skills.action: State the reach and result of separately treated statutory provisions, claims, or legal capacities separately; do not transfer a conclusion about one to a companion provision or claim without source support.

all_of: The source analyzes at least two statutory provisions, claims, or legal capacities and treats their scope or consequences separately.

preserve: Preserve any source-stated difference in the legal reach or outcome of companion provisions or claims.
Do not imply that a holding about one statutory scheme resolves a separately analyzed scheme unless the source does so.

skills.name: Source-supplied doctrinal labels
skills.action: Use source-supplied legal category labels to distinguish separate grounds or rules when those labels appear in the summary.

all_of: The source excerpt supplies a recognized legal category or doctrinal label and uses it to distinguish separate grounds or rules in its account of the holding.
exclude_if: The source excerpt supplies no recognized legal category or doctrinal label for distinguishing separate grounds or rules in its account of the holding.

preserve: Use only labels supported by the source, and preserve the distinction between separate legal grounds when the source makes one.

skills.name: Attribute reported arguments and concessions
skills.action: When reporting a litigant’s or agency’s material argument or concession, identify it as that party’s position rather than presenting it as the court’s own conclusion.

all_of: The source states a material argument, contention, or concession by a party or agency.

preserve: Do not turn an argument or concession into a holding of the court.
Preserve who made the position when reporting it.

skills.name: Attribute litigant positions and lower-court rulings
skills.action: Attribute contested positions to the party advancing them, distinguishing litigant arguments from the court’s conclusions.

all_of: The source identifies a litigant’s argument, claim, or position on an issue.

preserve: Do not present a party’s contention or a lower court’s ruling as the reviewing court’s holding.

skills.name: Retain governing legal labels and provision references
skills.action: Retain the relevant statutory subsection, constitutional provision, or established doctrinal label when stating the governing rule.

all_of: The source identifies the relevant rule by a statutory provision, constitutional provision, or doctrinal term.

preserve: Use the provision or doctrinal label for the rule actually discussed in the source; do not imply that a cited provision independently establishes a broader rule.

skills.name: Retention of operative legal terminology
skills.action: Retain recognizable statutory or doctrinal terms that carry the source's operative legal meaning, rather than replacing them with a looser everyday paraphrase.

all_of: The source uses a named statutory or doctrinal term as part of the issue, rule, or application.

preserve: Use a legal term only where it accurately reflects the source's usage and the proposition being summarized.
Do not treat a term appearing in one case as mandatory in other cases.

skills.name: Retain recognizable names for governing statutes and doctrines
skills.action: When stating a central rule, retain the recognizable name or doctrinal label of the governing statute or doctrine when the source supplies one, rather than describing the rule only in generic terms.

all_of: The source identifies a statute or doctrine by name or established label and uses it as a basis for resolving the dispute.
The source states the corresponding legal rule.

preserve: Use the correct statutory or doctrinal name and state its rule consistently with the source.
This is a terminology choice, not a requirement to quote the source or include every authority it discusses.

skills.name: Preserve operative wording in text-centered disputes
skills.action: When a rule’s scope turns on the wording of a statute, treaty, or established doctrine, retain its distinctive operative terms in a quotation or close paraphrase while compressing surrounding explanation.

all_of: The source interprets or applies a statute, treaty, or established doctrine.
The source makes the wording of the governing rule material to the dispute.
exclude_if: The source resolves the dispute without relying on the wording of a governing rule.

preserve: Do not broaden or narrow the rule while paraphrasing its wording.
Preserve a qualification or defined legal term when it determines the rule’s scope.

skills.name: Identify the operative statutory provision
skills.action: Name the operative statute or statutory provision when stating a holding that turns on its application.

all_of: The source identifies a statute or statutory provision as governing the dispute and applies it to reach a holding.
exclude_if: The source does not identify an operative statute or provision for the holding.

preserve: If naming a provision, preserve its correct scope and distinguish it from other statutes or constitutional provisions discussed in the source.

skills.name: Retain short operative legal phrases
skills.action: When a compact proposition turns on a distinctive operative statutory, contractual, or procedural phrase, retain that short phrase in the proposition, quoting it where the summary does so, rather than replacing it with a less specific generality.

all_of: The source text expressly quotes statutory or contractual language and explains how that language governs a legal issue.

preserve: Retain a phrase only when it is present in the source and relevant to the proposition.
Preserve the phrase’s legal function and surrounding proposition accurately; do not imply that every source quotation should be reproduced.

skills.name: Formal title for the governing enactment
skills.action: Identify the governing enactment by its formal title when naming the statutory framework.

all_of: The source identifies a governing statute by its formal title.
The source’s legal analysis or result is based on that statute.

preserve: Keep the named enactment tied to the proposition or statutory provisions the source associates with it.
Do not add a statute title or provision absent from the source.

skills.name: Paraphrasing quoted statutory or regulatory wording
skills.action: When the source quotes statutory or regulatory wording at length, state its operative effect in concise paraphrase rather than reproducing the quoted text.

all_of: The source quotes statutory or regulatory wording relevant to the decision.
The court applies or interprets that wording.

preserve: Preserve the legal effect the court attributes to the text; paraphrase must not broaden or narrow the court's interpretation.

skills.name: Paraphrase extended reasoning compactly
skills.action: Render extended doctrinal explanation as compact paraphrase instead of reproducing long source passages verbatim.

all_of: The source develops a rule or rationale through extended explanation, quotation, or rhetorical elaboration.

preserve: Retain the substance and qualifications of a rationale when compressing it; do not treat any particular quotation or example as mandatory.

skills.name: State the scope qualification that resolves the dispute
skills.action: When the holding’s reach turns on a contested limitation or exception, state the qualification that answers that dispute instead of leaving the governing rule overbroad.

all_of: The source addresses a proposed limitation, exception, or distinction affecting the scope of the governing rule.
exclude_if: The source does not address a contested limitation or scope distinction.

preserve: Preserve whether the rule is mandatory, optional, conditional, or subject to the asserted exception; do not imply broader reach than the source supports.

skills.name: Keep legal positions attributed
skills.action: Attribute positions and conclusions to the party or court that advanced them, especially when describing a lower court's analysis before the reviewing court's response.

all_of: The source excerpt presents a party's position or a lower court's conclusion that is material to the decision.

preserve: Do not recast a party's contention or a lower court's holding as the reviewing court's own conclusion.

skills.name: Preserve consequential legal distinctions
skills.action: Retain distinctions between neighboring legal questions or theories when the source makes those distinctions consequential; do not collapse them into a single undifferentiated issue.

all_of: The source expressly distinguishes legal questions, claims, or theories relevant to the decision.

preserve: State accurately which issue or theory was decided and which, if any, was left open.

skills.name: Bounded statement of the holding
skills.action: Use a concise, explicit holding statement to identify the court’s resolution, and keep the stated rule tied to the issue actually decided.

all_of: The source resolves an issue through a legal holding or conclusion.

preserve: Preserve the holding’s legal subject, conditions, and degree of certainty; a concise formulation must not broaden the source’s conclusion.

skills.name: Retain limiting conditions on a holding
skills.action: When the source makes the result depend on a defined factual or procedural category, retain that category in the stated holding rather than presenting the ruling as categorical.

all_of: The source limits its decision to a described application, group, or procedural posture.

preserve: Preserve material limits on who, what application, or which procedural question the court decided; do not imply that an undecided merits question was resolved.

skills.name: Identify the controlling legal framework
skills.action: Name the governing statute or constitutional provision in the summary's statement of the result when the source makes that legal framework central to the decision.

all_of: The source identifies a statute or constitutional provision as the framework for the issue decided.

preserve: Accurately identify the provision and its role; include it only when the source supports that connection.

skills.name: Preserve limits on the holding
skills.action: Retain a material limit or qualification in the holding when the source makes the legal result conditional or narrower than a categorical rule.

all_of: The source’s substantive conclusion is expressly qualified by context, a procedural condition, or a limitation on the remedy or right.

preserve: Do not broaden a case-specific or remedial proposition into a categorical rule; retain the stated condition or limit when expressing it.

skills.name: Retain the source's stated limits on the rule
skills.action: When the source rejects an overbroad interpretation or states a limiting condition, include that boundary in the summary's account of the rule.

all_of: The source resolves the dispute by rejecting a categorical reading, stating a limiting condition, or distinguishing the challenged conduct from conduct the law forbids.

preserve: Do not turn a fact-dependent standard into an automatic rule or a limited holding into a categorical one.

skills.name: Make the disposition explicit
skills.action: State the court's actual disposition explicitly, usually as the concluding result of the summary.

all_of: The source states the court's disposition.

preserve: State the result and any material condition or limitation accurately.
Distinguish the current court's disposition from a lower court's earlier ruling.

skills.name: Distinguish court holdings from litigant positions
skills.action: Attribute resolved propositions to the court, and identify a party's or agency's position as such when reporting it, rather than presenting a contested position as an established holding.

all_of: The source states a court's resolution of a legal issue.
The source states a party's or agency's position on that issue.

preserve: Do not imply that an argument or agency position was adopted by the court unless the source says so.
Where the summary reports only the holding, it need not reproduce the parties' arguments.

skills.name: Attribute reviewed positions to their source
skills.action: Attribute a reviewed court’s ruling or an agency’s stated rationale to that actor, distinguishing it from the reviewing court’s own holding.

all_of: The source describes a lower-court ruling or agency position that the reviewing court considers.
exclude_if: The available source excerpt contains no separate prior ruling or agency position.

preserve: If reporting a lower-court conclusion or an agency’s rationale, preserve who made that claim and distinguish it from the reviewing court’s conclusion.

skills.name: Retain express limits on rules and holdings
skills.action: When the source expressly limits a rule or holding through an exception, qualification, or boundary, retain that limit when stating the proposition; do not present the proposition as broader than the source does.

all_of: The source states a legal rule or holding and expressly identifies a qualification, exception, or boundary on its scope.
exclude_if: The supplied source view does not show an express qualification, exception, or boundary for the proposition.

preserve: Preserve the source's qualifications when stating the proposition, if that proposition is included.
Do not convert a rule tied to particular circumstances into an unrestricted rule.

skills.name: Attribute disputed positions and lower-court conclusions
skills.action: Keep contested assertions, arguments, and lower-court conclusions attributed to the party or court that made them; do not present them as the summarizing court’s own findings.

all_of: The source distinguishes a party's argument or allegation from a court's finding or holding, or distinguishes a lower-court conclusion from the reviewing court's decision.

preserve: Preserve whether a proposition was alleged, argued, or decided, and identify the relevant party or court when the source does so.
Do not turn a lower-court ruling or a party's position into the reviewing court's holding.

skills.name: Preserve limiting conditions on the holding
skills.action: When a holding depends on a limiting circumstance, evidentiary gap, or rejected inference, state the consequence with that qualification rather than turning it into an unqualified rule.

all_of: The opinion resolves an issue by explaining what a circumstance or evidentiary condition does—or does not—establish.

preserve: Keep the stated evidentiary or factual qualification accurate when retaining the proposition.
Do not imply that the cited circumstance alone proves or defeats a claim when the opinion says it does not.

skills.name: Bound holdings to the legal provision or doctrine
skills.action: State holdings within the specific constitutional, statutory, or doctrinal boundary addressed in the source, rather than recasting them as broader rules.

all_of: The source states a holding tied to an identifiable constitutional provision, statute, or doctrinal category.

preserve: When the source limits a conclusion to a particular statute, constitutional provision, remedy, or procedural question, preserve that limitation if stating the conclusion.
Do not imply a broader rule than the source decides.

skills.name: Attribute reviewed reasoning to the lower court
skills.action: When recounting a lower court’s reasoning that is under review, identify it as that court’s position rather than presenting it as the summarizing court’s own holding.

all_of: The source describes a lower court’s reasoning or conclusion on an issue addressed by the decision being summarized.

preserve: Keep the lower court’s rationale distinct from the decision being summarized, especially where the latter rejects, reverses, or otherwise reviews that rationale.

skills.name: Retain material uncertainty and belief markers
skills.action: Retain explicit markers of uncertainty, belief, or probability when reporting a material factual premise, rather than turning it into a certain fact.

all_of: The source explicitly qualifies a material factual premise with an uncertainty, belief, or probability marker.

preserve: Keep uncertainty attached to the proposition it qualifies, and distinguish a party’s belief or a possible outcome from an established fact.

skills.name: Attribute relevant lower-court determinations
skills.action: When reporting a lower-court finding or ruling used in the reviewing court’s account, attribute it to the lower court instead of presenting it as an unqualified finding of the reviewing court.

all_of: The source recounts a distinct lower-court finding or ruling that is relevant to the reviewing court’s discussion.
exclude_if: The source contains no relevant lower-court finding or ruling.

preserve: Do not attribute a lower-court finding or holding to the reviewing court.
If a lower-court determination is included, preserve which court made it and whether it was a finding, ruling, or holding.

skills.name: Preserve stated limits on a rule’s reach
skills.action: State express boundaries on a rule’s reach, such as which claims or parties it covers, what condition triggers it, or when it ends, rather than presenting the rule as categorical.

all_of: The source states a legal rule with an express subject-matter, party, causal, evidentiary, or temporal boundary.
exclude_if: The source states no express boundary relevant to the rule being summarized.

preserve: Retain the direction and extent of a limitation, including any stated triggering condition or endpoint.
Do not convert a case-specific or qualified rule into a universal prohibition or entitlement.

skills.name: Keep disputed positions attributed
skills.action: When the opinion reports a party’s disputed factual or legal position as a claim, contention, or allegation, retain its attributed status rather than presenting it as an established fact or the court’s conclusion.

all_of: The source identifies a disputed position as a party’s claim, contention, allegation, or defense.
exclude_if: The source presents the proposition as an undisputed fact or as the court’s own finding.

preserve: Preserve whether the source describes a proposition as a party’s allegation or argument, rather than as an established fact or judicial determination.
Do not strengthen or weaken the source’s stated degree of certainty.

skills.name: Name legally material party categories
skills.action: When a party’s or property’s legal category is material to the rule being applied, identify that category in the summary rather than describing the dispute only in generic terms.

all_of: The source identifies a party or property by a legal or institutional category that matters to the disputed rule or its application.
exclude_if: The source does not make a party’s or property’s legal category relevant to the dispute.

preserve: Retain the category that makes the rule relevant, such as the type of property, service-member status, or foreign-litigant status, when the source makes that category legally significant.
Do not add a category or legal consequence that the source does not support.

skills.name: Anchor statutory holdings to the identified provision
skills.action: When a holding turns on an identified statute or statutory provision, name that provision or its statutory source in the summary’s statement of the holding.

all_of: The source identifies a statute or specific statutory provision as the basis of a principal issue or holding.
exclude_if: The supplied source view does not identify a statutory basis for the principal issue or holding.

preserve: If the source identifies a particular statutory provision as controlling, preserve the distinction between that provision and other provisions or legal issues.
Retain statutory identifiers only when they are available in the source.

skills.name: Attribute litigant contentions and distinguish the court’s response
skills.action: When the source evaluates a litigant’s contention, identify it as that litigant’s contention and report the court’s response, rather than recasting the contention as an accepted premise.

all_of: The source identifies a party’s contention or argument and the court expressly accepts, rejects, or distinguishes it.
exclude_if: The supplied source view states a rule without identifying a party contention or the court’s response to one.

preserve: Keep party arguments distinct from the court’s own conclusions.
Preserve the source’s attribution when reporting who advanced a contention.

skills.name: Retain operative limits and triggers
skills.action: When summarizing a rule or test, retain operative conditions, thresholds, and triggers that define its scope, including who must act, what standard applies, and when the duty or rule applies.

all_of: The source states a legal rule or test with an express condition, threshold, burden, or trigger.

preserve: Keep the source’s allocation of burdens, conditions, and threshold language accurate if the proposition is included.

skills.name: Preserve the source’s level of certainty
skills.action: Preserve the source’s degree of certainty when describing an inference or rationale; do not turn a tentative, qualified, or unresolved proposition into a categorical one.

all_of: The source expresses uncertainty, probability, qualification, or an unresolved interpretive point in reasoning relevant to the decision.

preserve: Use certainty, probability, and qualification consistently with the source; do not imply that a particular tentative rationale is the holding unless the source does so.

skills.name: Use formal declarative summary prose
skills.action: Use impersonal, declarative legal-summary prose to state the propositions and their consequences.

all_of: The source reports judicial reasoning, a holding, or a disposition.

preserve: Maintain the source's legal meaning and attribution while using a neutral reporting voice.

skills.name: Maintain a neutral reporting voice
skills.action: Report the court's decision in neutral third-person language rather than adopting first-person commentary or rhetorical phrasing from separate judicial remarks.

all_of: The source includes a dissent, concurrence, or other expressly separate judicial commentary.

preserve: Attribute a separate opinion's position if it is included.
Do not misstate a separate opinion as the court's holding.

skills.name: Use impersonal case-reporting voice
skills.action: Report the court, parties, or agency in an impersonal third-person legal-reporting voice rather than addressing the reader directly.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion resolving a dispute.

preserve: Keep attribution clear when reporting a party’s contention, an agency action, or the court’s own conclusion.

skills.name: Impersonal reporting of judicial conclusions
skills.action: Render the Court’s conclusions in an impersonal, court-centered reporting voice rather than carrying over first-person judicial narration.

all_of: The source excerpt states the court's conclusion or holding with first-person judicial narration (for example, “we hold”).
The source excerpt provides a conclusion that can be reported without first-person wording.
exclude_if: The available source excerpt contains no judicial conclusion to report.

preserve: Keep the conclusion attributed to the court or agency identified in the source; do not turn a court’s conclusion into an unqualified general rule.

skills.name: Impersonal reporting of judicial conclusions
skills.action: Use an impersonal case-reporting voice to state the court’s conclusions rather than carrying over first-person judicial narration.

all_of: The source uses first-person judicial narration for a conclusion or evaluation.

preserve: Keep the court’s conclusion and its scope accurate when converting first-person narration to impersonal reporting.

skills.name: Convert first-person judicial narration to impersonal reporting
skills.action: When the source narrates the Court’s work in the first person, recast that narration as impersonal reporting about the court or the case rather than carrying over “we” or “our.”

all_of: The source contains first-person judicial narration about the Court’s task, analysis, or decision.
exclude_if: The source does not use first-person judicial narration.

preserve: Keep the Court’s position and the source’s attribution accurate when shifting from first-person narration to institutional or impersonal phrasing.

skills.name: Use impersonal case-reporting language
skills.action: Express the court’s conclusions in an impersonal case-reporting voice, rather than carrying over the opinion’s first-person judicial narration.

all_of: The source expresses a ruling or reasoning in the court’s own narrative voice, including first-person phrasing.

preserve: State the result and governing proposition accurately.
Do not imply that the opinion itself uses the summary’s reporting formulation.

skills.name: Impersonal decision-reporting voice
skills.action: Use an impersonal legal-reporting voice, phrasing the entry as a decision or proposition rather than addressing the reader or narrating a personal reaction.

all_of: The supplied source is a judicial opinion that states a legal determination, ruling, or disposition.
exclude_if: The supplied material is not a judicial decision or does not state a determination to report.

preserve: Keep the identity and action of the deciding court accurate when the summary names or attributes a ruling to it.
Do not convert a source’s qualified or mixed result into an unqualified one merely to maintain a declarative style.

skills.name: Use party-role labels
skills.action: Identify litigants by their procedural or legally relevant capacity (for example, appellants, cargo owners, or truck owner) rather than adding or repeating personal names.

all_of: The source identifies parties by litigation role or legally relevant capacity.

preserve: Keep the party's role accurate where the summary uses a role label; do not substitute a different party or capacity.

skills.name: Impersonal case-reporting voice
skills.action: Use detached, impersonal case-reporting statements rather than addressing the reader or adding authorial commentary.

all_of: The source is a court opinion or court order.

preserve: Keep any retained attribution or description of the court's action accurate; the impersonal register does not require omitting a stated participant or qualification.

skills.name: Impersonal case-summary voice
skills.action: When the source uses first-person judicial narration to announce a decision, report the ruling in an impersonal case-summary voice rather than retaining the judge's or court's first-person voice.

all_of: The source uses first-person judicial narration to state the ruling or disposition.

preserve: Preserve who granted or denied relief and the source's stated procedural conditions; changing voice should not change the actor or result.

skills.name: Quote short operative phrases selectively
skills.action: Use quotation marks selectively for short operative or disputed phrases drawn from the source; do not reproduce extended source quotations merely because the opinion quotes them at length.

all_of: The source expressly quotes or analyzes a distinctive operative phrase, statutory term, or disputed wording.

preserve: If a quoted phrase is retained, preserve its wording and legal context accurately.
Do not treat any particular quoted phrase as required content.

skills.name: Use impersonal formulations for judicial conclusions
skills.action: Render the court’s conclusions as impersonal legal propositions rather than carrying over the opinion’s first-person judicial narration.

all_of: The source uses first-person judicial narration when stating or explaining a legal conclusion.

preserve: Preserve which court or actor made a conclusion when attribution is material.
Do not erase a source distinction between the court’s holding and a party’s contention.

skills.name: Maintain an impersonal case-digest register
skills.action: Use formal, impersonal case-reporting prose, referring to parties by their litigation roles rather than addressing the reader.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion.

preserve: Party roles, allegations, and judicial conclusions must remain distinguishable; impersonal phrasing must not blur who made a claim or reached a conclusion.

skills.name: Use an impersonal reporting voice
skills.action: Report judicial reasoning in an impersonal, third-person summary voice rather than adopting the source judge’s first-person narration.

all_of: The source uses first-person judicial narration or rhetorical commentary.

preserve: Maintain the court’s attribution and do not turn its holding or reasoning into the summary writer’s independent assertion.

skills.name: Restrained doctrinal reporting
skills.action: Use a restrained doctrinal reporting voice when condensing argumentative or rhetorical passages.

all_of: The source contains rhetorical characterization, pointed criticism, or argumentative asides relevant to the discussion.

preserve: Preserve the substance and force of the court's reasoning even when reducing rhetorical language.

skills.name: Use impersonal judicial-summary register
skills.action: Use impersonal, court-centered legal prose to report claims, rules, and conclusions rather than addressing the reader or adopting conversational commentary.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion.

preserve: Keep the source's level of certainty and attribute conclusions to the appropriate court or party.

skills.name: Maintain an impersonal case-reporting voice
skills.action: Use an impersonal case-reporting voice to describe the parties, court action, and holdings, rather than addressing the reader or presenting advice.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion reporting a decision.

preserve: Identify the court's determination as a holding or result when needed to distinguish it from a party's contention.

skills.name: Report judicial reasoning in third person
skills.action: Recast the source's judicial first-person voice as a neutral third-person report of the court's action or reasoning.

all_of: The source uses first-person judicial language to describe the court's action or reasoning.

preserve: Retain the source's attribution when identifying a particular court or justice.
Do not change the degree of certainty or the substance of the court's statement when converting its voice.

skills.name: Retain the stated basis for the decision
skills.action: Include the source's stated legal basis when the summary sets out why the result follows, linking the rule or rationale to the issue being resolved.

all_of: The source states a legal or interpretive basis for its decision.
exclude_if: The available source material does not provide a stated basis for the relevant conclusion.

preserve: Represent the source's rationale accurately and in connection with the proposition it supports.
Do not add a rationale merely because it would make the holding more explanatory.

skills.name: Select facts that locate the dispute
skills.action: Use a small amount of case-specific factual context to identify the transaction, property, or agency action to which the holding applies.

all_of: The source provides facts that distinguish the matter being decided.
exclude_if: The source view does not include enough factual context to identify the relevant transaction or action.

preserve: Keep the facts tied to the issue and result in the source; do not turn an example or party-specific detail into a general requirement.
Maintain accuracy about who acted, what was at issue, and any legally material condition.

skills.name: Report the stated case result
skills.action: Include the operative case result when the source states it, distinguishing a reversal from a vacatur and remand or other stated procedural outcome.

all_of: The source states the court's operative result or the action to be taken in the case.
exclude_if: The available source material does not state an operative result.

preserve: Use the operative result stated in the source and distinguish the disposition from the substantive rule.
Do not infer a procedural result from the merits holding alone.

skills.name: State the principal resolution
skills.action: State the bottom-line resolution of the principal legal challenge, and include the stated case disposition when it is available in the summary material.

all_of: The source resolves a principal legal challenge or states a case disposition.

preserve: Distinguish the result on the principal challenge from subsidiary rulings and the formal appellate disposition.
Do not imply that a lower-court ruling was affirmed or reversed unless the source supports that result.

skills.name: Select the operative rationale
skills.action: Compress supporting reasoning into the principal rationale that connects the governing rule to its application, rather than reproducing extended source discussion.

all_of: The source develops reasoning beyond the statement of the holding.

preserve: Keep the selected rationale faithful to the source and retain any qualification necessary to explain why the rule applies.

skills.name: Condense extended legal reasoning
skills.action: Condense extended reasoning into a direct legal proposition, retaining a concise explanation where it materially supports the result.

all_of: The source develops a legal conclusion through extended analysis or multiple supporting reasons.

preserve: If an explanation is retained, preserve the source's reasoning and degree of certainty; do not imply that a selected rationale is the sole basis unless the source says so.

skills.name: Report the disposition
skills.action: Include the stated case outcome, commonly as a brief closing disposition.

all_of: The source states the court's disposition of the case or appeal.

preserve: Match the disposition to the source, including whether the judgment was affirmed, reversed, dismissed, or remanded.

skills.name: Retain facts that condition the application
skills.action: Include a concrete factual predicate when the source makes the holding turn on particular conduct, evidence, or application of a rule.

all_of: The source expressly connects a holding to case-specific conduct, evidence, or application facts.

preserve: Retained facts must reflect the source and must not be presented as broader factual requirements than the holding supports.

skills.name: Compress the factual setup
skills.action: Give a compact factual setup that identifies the parties' relevant relationship or transaction and the facts that frame the legal dispute, rather than recreating the full narrative.

all_of: The source provides a factual account of the parties or events underlying the dispute.
The source contains more factual detail than is needed to identify the dispute addressed in the summary.

preserve: Retain the facts that identify the dispute and materially frame the legal question when they are stated.
Do not import details that are not available in the source.

skills.name: Choose contextual facts that explain the dispute
skills.action: Retain a small set of contextual facts that explains how the legal dispute arose, including the fact or relationship that makes the rule consequential in the case.

all_of: The source supplies factual context relevant to the legal dispute or its application.

preserve: If a fact is retained, preserve its role and relationship accurately; do not substitute an illustrative source fact for a required fact in other cases.
Avoid implying that every detail in the source is material to the summary.

skills.name: Connect the rule to its application
skills.action: Present a governing rule alongside its case-specific consequence or application when the summary reports both, keeping the connection concise.

all_of: The source gives a general legal rule and applies it to the facts or circumstances before the court.

preserve: If stating a rule and its application, retain the source's qualifying conditions and case-specific basis accurately.
Do not treat a supporting reason as a separate mandatory proposition in cases where the source does not use it.

skills.name: Make the controlling legal conclusion explicit
skills.action: State the controlling legal conclusion as a direct proposition, rather than leaving the reader to infer it from procedural history or background.

all_of: The source resolves a legal issue by stating a rule, limitation, or application of law.

preserve: Retain the scope and qualifications of the source's conclusion; do not turn a limited holding into a broader rule.
Distinguish the court's holding from arguments made by parties or lower courts.

skills.name: Center the specific legal classification
skills.action: Frame the dispute around the specific legal classification the court resolves, rather than broad background questions that do not define the holding.

all_of: The source identifies a particular legal classification, statutory phrase, or boundary as the question decided.

preserve: State the classification and its scope accurately; do not broaden a narrow interpretive question into a general statement about the field.

skills.name: State the narrow decisional hinge
skills.action: Frame the dispute around the narrow legal question or decisional hinge the source identifies, rather than describing only the broader subject of the case.

all_of: The source expressly identifies a particular legal question, threshold, or distinction as the matter for decision.
exclude_if: The source excerpt states no identifiable question or decisional hinge.

preserve: Keep the stated issue distinct from broader legal questions or claims that the source does not resolve.
Do not recast a threshold ruling as a decision on the underlying constitutional or statutory merits.

skills.name: Retain the procedural frame for relief
skills.action: Identify the procedural or threshold doctrine that frames the Court’s decision when it limits the route to relief, and distinguish it from the underlying claim.

all_of: The source makes a procedural or threshold framework—such as immunity or collateral-review limits—material to the Court’s decision.
exclude_if: The source decides the dispute without a material procedural or threshold framework.

preserve: State the framework accurately and do not imply that a procedural ruling necessarily resolves the underlying claim on its merits.
Include a framework only when it materially explains the result in the source.

skills.name: Frame the issue through its resolution
skills.action: State the legal proposition that resolves the issue, rather than restating the source's question presented.

all_of: The source expressly frames an issue or question for decision.
The source reaches a legal conclusion resolving that issue.

preserve: Retain the source's actual conclusion and its operative limits; do not imply a resolution where the source leaves the issue open.

skills.name: Name the enactment grounding a stated legal conclusion
skills.action: Identify the governing statute or constitutional provision when the summary states a legal conclusion that the source grounds in that enactment.

all_of: The source expressly grounds a material holding or legal conclusion in an identifiable statute or constitutional provision.

preserve: Name only an enactment identified in the source, and keep its role in the conclusion accurate; do not imply that a provision supplies a holding the source does not make.

skills.name: Connect legal principles to their application
skills.action: Express the governing rule or interpretive principle and connect it to the case-specific application or consequence.

all_of: The source supplies a legal rule or interpretive principle and applies it to facts or a disputed consequence.

preserve: If the rule or application is retained, preserve its direction and the source’s stated relationship between the rule and the consequence.

skills.name: Select facts that connect the rule to its application
skills.action: Include case-specific facts that explain why the governing rule applies to the parties’ dispute, while selecting rather than reproducing the full factual narrative.

all_of: The source applies a legal rule to particular facts.
The source view provides facts relevant to that application.
exclude_if: The source’s resolution is independent of any case-specific factual application.

preserve: Retain the facts necessary to understand the court’s application and avoid converting an illustrative case fact into a general legal requirement.

skills.name: Choose dispute-linked facts for the setup
skills.action: Select facts that situate the dispute and connect it to the legal question, often presenting the key transaction or conduct alongside the pertinent procedural event.

all_of: The source supplies factual background relevant to a legal dispute.

preserve: If a fact is retained, preserve the relevant parties, sequence, and material qualification accurately.
Do not treat any one case’s factual detail as required in other summaries.

skills.name: Select operative case-specific facts
skills.action: Select a few case-specific facts that make the dispute and the practical stakes intelligible, rather than retelling every factual detail in the source.

all_of: The source describes the events or conduct giving rise to the dispute.
exclude_if: The supplied source contains no case-specific factual background.

preserve: If a factual detail is retained, preserve who did what and the legally relevant relationship between that event and the claim.

skills.name: State the disposition
skills.action: State the case’s stated disposition, often near the close of the summary, using the appropriate result for the judgment under review.

all_of: The source provides a disposition or a remedy ordered by the Court.
exclude_if: The supplied source excerpt does not identify the disposition or remedy.

preserve: Distinguish the Court’s disposition from the lower court’s ruling and describe any conditional or discretionary remedy accurately.

skills.name: Explicit principal resolution
skills.action: State the court’s principal legal resolution explicitly in the holding portion, rather than leaving it only implicit in the supporting analysis.

all_of: The source presents a legal question or dispute that the court resolves.

preserve: Preserve which legal issue the resolution addresses and any stated limits on that resolution.

skills.name: Represent distinct secondary rulings in multi-question opinions
skills.action: When the opinion resolves several distinct legal questions, include separately stated secondary rulings or rules alongside the principal result, selecting those the summary treats as independent propositions.

all_of: The source resolves at least two separately identifiable legal questions or states distinct legal rules.

preserve: Do not imply that every argument or subsidiary observation must be included.
If a secondary ruling is included, preserve its scope and relationship to the source’s principal result.

skills.name: State interpretive reasoning compactly
skills.action: When the opinion states a general interpretive rule or a distinct construction rationale, express it as a compact proposition rather than reproducing the full analysis.

all_of: The source expressly states a general interpretive rule or a distinct rationale for construing a statute, contract, or other legal text.

preserve: If reporting an interpretive rule or rationale, preserve the source’s stated scope and do not turn a case-specific application into a broader rule.

skills.name: Compress extended reasoning into rule and application
skills.action: Express the controlling reasoning as a concise rule tied to its application, rather than reproducing the source's extended argumentative development or strings of supporting quotations.

all_of: The source develops a holding through extended analysis, examples, or quoted authorities.

preserve: If stating a reason, preserve its relation to the source's holding and do not enlarge the holding beyond the application the court decided.

skills.name: Select facts tied to the legal issue
skills.action: Retain the factual predicates that make the rule's application understandable, while leaving out incidental detail that does not affect the stated result.

all_of: The source supplies factual background in addition to the legal issue and ruling.

preserve: Preserve the legally operative status, timing, or conduct when retained; do not imply that an example or omitted fact was immaterial to the court unless the source supports that characterization.

skills.name: Compact statement of the operative holding
skills.action: State the case’s operative legal conclusion in a compact holding, connecting the rule or legal effect to the issue the court resolved.

all_of: The source states a substantive legal conclusion by the reviewing court.
exclude_if: The source records only a procedural disposition without a substantive ruling.

preserve: If the source makes the result depend on a stated condition, context, or legal standard, retain that qualification rather than turn the holding into an unconditional rule.

skills.name: Select facts that frame the dispute
skills.action: Include a small number of facts that identify the dispute or the event giving rise to the ruling; leave out factual particulars that do not help frame that issue.

all_of: The source recounts facts underlying a substantive dispute.

preserve: If a fact is included, keep its source-supported role and attribution; do not add factual details unavailable in the source.

skills.name: Report the order or decree entry
skills.action: State the procedural or decree-entry outcome in a compact form, such as that certiorari was granted and the judgment vacated, or that a decree was entered.

all_of: The source is a Supreme Court order, opinion, or decree that grants, vacates, remands, or enters a decree.

preserve: If stating a disposition, retain its actual procedural action; do not treat a decree-entry date as specifying the decree's substantive terms.

skills.name: Select the operative factual setting
skills.action: State the concrete circumstances that make the dispute intelligible, selecting the conduct or condition directly connected to the legal question rather than reproducing every record detail.

all_of: The source describes concrete conduct or conditions underlying the dispute.
The source includes concrete circumstances connected to the dispute’s legal question or requested relief.

preserve: Keep any retained factual detail accurate, including who acted, what happened, and the circumstance that connects the event to the dispute.
Do not treat any particular training-case fact as mandatory.

skills.name: Compress the explanation to the rationale for the action
skills.action: Compress the court's explanation to the rule, application, or unresolved question that accounts for its action instead of reproducing the full reasoning discussion.

all_of: The source states reasoning that accounts for the court's action.

preserve: Preserve qualifications, uncertainty, and the distinction between an issue the court decides and one it leaves open.
If stating the rationale, do not turn an illustrative rule or preliminary question into a definitive holding.

skills.name: Retain scope-defining distinctions between actors or statuses
skills.action: When the decision’s scope turns on a distinction between legal actors or statuses, state the relevant categories separately instead of treating them as interchangeable.

all_of: The source distinguishes two or more actors, entities, or legal statuses that affect the scope of the issue or rule.

preserve: Represent the source’s distinction accurately; do not imply that a rule governing one actor or status automatically governs another.

skills.name: Identify litigants through legally relevant roles
skills.action: Describe litigants by their legally relevant roles or relationships—such as petitioner, respondent, State, agency, or affected employees—and use an individual’s name when it helps identify the case or a later reference.

all_of: The source identifies litigants by both personal or institutional names and their legal roles or relationships.

preserve: Retain names or relationships needed to distinguish parties or explain the legal dispute; this convention does not require omitting names.

skills.name: Compact supporting-precedent citations
skills.action: When including a supporting precedent, present it as a compact legal citation rather than reproducing the source’s full string of parallel reporter citations.

all_of: The source cites supporting judicial decisions and supplies reporter information for them.

preserve: Use accurate citation information supported by the source if a precedent is cited.
Treat compact citations as an observed presentation choice, not a requirement to cite a precedent or include a page pinpoint.

skills.name: Plain-prose presentation
skills.action: Use plain prose presentation without Markdown headings or bullet markers; proposition numbering may still be used.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion.

preserve: Do not treat ordinary proposition numbering as Markdown or as inconsistent with plain prose.

skills.name: Inline legal-authority references
skills.action: When including a legal authority reference, place it within the relevant prose proposition or its closing disposition rather than presenting a separate citation list.

all_of: The source identifies statutes, code provisions, or cases relevant to its legal propositions.

preserve: Only include authorities supported by the source, and reproduce names, statutory references, and citations accurately when retained.
Do not make any particular citation or page reference mandatory when it is unavailable in the source or not selected by the summary.

skills.name: Pair available lower-court citations with the closing disposition
skills.action: When the source supplies a lower-court reporter citation and a disposition, include the available citation in the closing disposition line, adjacent to the disposition.

all_of: The source supplies an identifiable lower-court reporter citation.
The source states a disposition.

preserve: Use only a citation supplied by the source, and keep the citation associated with the correct lower-court decision.

skills.name: Direct proposition presentation without a separate heading
skills.action: Present the digest propositions directly, without a separate question-style title or case-description heading.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion that resolves a legal question.

preserve: Do not treat this observed heading choice as a requirement to use any particular numbering style.
If an issue heading is retained, preserve the distinction between a heading and the legal proposition itself.

skills.name: Inline statutory identifiers
skills.action: When identifying a governing enactment in the summary, place its concise identifying citation within the prose proposition rather than reproducing extended statutory text.

all_of: The source grounds the determination in an identified statute or statutory provision.
The source supplies an enactment or provision identifier.

preserve: Use only enactment names, sections, and citation details available in the source.
Do not imply that every summary must include a statutory citation when the human summary does not identify one.

skills.name: Close with a concise affirmance citation
skills.action: For a source reporting one lower-court judgment affirmed and supplying its citation, close with a concise lower-court citation followed by the affirmance.

all_of: The source reports a single judgment under review and states that it is affirmed.
The source supplies a citation for the lower-court judgment.
exclude_if: The source reports multiple appeals or distinct dispositions.

preserve: State the correct disposition and use only a lower-court citation available in the source.
Do not apply this pattern when the source has multiple appeals or distinct dispositions.

skills.name: Unnumbered prose for a single principal resolution
skills.action: For a source organized around one principal legal resolution, present the summary as unnumbered prose rather than dividing it into numbered propositions.

all_of: The source states one principal legal resolution rather than separately presenting several independent propositions.
exclude_if: The source presents multiple independent propositions as distinct holdings or rules.

preserve: If the summary states a legal proposition, preserve its stated scope and qualifications.

skills.name: Direct proposition format
skills.action: Present the summary as direct, court-centered legal propositions rather than adding question headings or an explanatory introduction.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion that states one or more legal propositions.

preserve: Keep any proposition’s legal effect accurate; this convention concerns presentation, not which holdings must be included.

skills.name: Use unheaded prose format
skills.action: Use unheaded prose rather than adding question headings, markdown headings, bullets, or reader-directed framing.

all_of: The source is presented as a judicial opinion or court case rather than as a form that itself requires a structured response.
exclude_if: Explicit source metadata or source content requires a particular heading or list format.

preserve: Keep the propositions readable and separated as needed without requiring a fixed number of paragraphs or sentences.

skills.name: Use continuous formal headnote prose
skills.action: Use concise, formal, declarative headnote prose in a continuous paragraph, without adding reader-directed language or decorative headings.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion represented by a legal-summary or headnote-style human summary.

preserve: Maintain accurate legal terms and necessary qualifications; compactness does not require omitting a material proposition or adopting a fixed word limit.

skills.name: Paraphrase extended quoted material
skills.action: Condense extended quoted passages—such as instructions, testimony, or quoted judicial reasoning—into a summary proposition instead of reproducing the passage at length; short operative phrases may remain.

all_of: The source contains an extended quotation that explains or applies a legal proposition.
The source contains the legal proposition or outcome associated with the quotation.

preserve: If a quotation or a detail from it is retained, preserve its meaning and attribution.
Do not omit an operative limitation or qualification merely because it appears within quoted material.

skills.name: Paraphrase quoted legal material
skills.action: Paraphrase quoted statutory or judicial material into the operative rule or proposition instead of reproducing the extended quotation.

all_of: The source includes quoted statutory language or an extended quotation from another judicial opinion.
The source also explains the legal effect of that material.
exclude_if: The precise quoted wording is itself the issue being summarized.

preserve: If quoted language is retained, preserve its wording and attribution accurately.
Preserve the legal effect and any qualifications the source draws from the quoted material.

skills.name: Compress citation trails
skills.action: Compress lengthy strings of cited authorities: retain a selected authority when the summary does so, but do not reproduce the source’s full citation trail.

all_of: The source includes citations to multiple authorities or a citation trail supporting a legal proposition.

preserve: If a cited authority is retained, preserve its identity and the proposition for which the source uses it.
Do not require a page reference or citation detail that is unavailable in the source.

skills.name: Compress procedural chronology
skills.action: Condense extended lower-court chronology and intermediate procedural events into the posture needed to understand the legal proposition, rather than recounting dates and steps in sequence.

all_of: The source recounts multiple procedural events, dates, or intermediate rulings before the court’s decision.

preserve: Retain the procedural vehicle and any procedural event that changes the rule, available relief, or disposition.

skills.name: Leave out nonessential litigation chronology
skills.action: Omit the sequence of litigation events when it is not needed to state the rule or outcome; do not substitute procedural chronology for the legal proposition.

all_of: The source excerpt recounts procedural events such as filing, trial, appeal, or prior litigation.
The source states a rule or conclusion independently of that chronology, without relying on the chronology as a premise of the rule.
exclude_if: The source makes elapsed time or a procedural event a stated condition or basis of the rule or outcome.

preserve: Retain timing or procedural facts when the source makes them part of the governing rule or necessary to distinguish the outcome.

skills.name: Omit competing arguments from a statement of the court’s conclusion
skills.action: Leave out the parties’ competing arguments and rejected positions when stating the court’s conclusion, rather than recasting those arguments as additional holdings.

all_of: The source describes competing party positions, objections, or arguments.
The source states a court conclusion or disposition distinct from the parties’ positions.

preserve: If an argument is retained, attribute it to the party advancing it and do not present it as the court’s holding.
Preserve a court’s express adoption or rejection of an argument when that disposition is part of the stated rule or result.

skills.name: Omit subsidiary factual particulars
skills.action: Leave out subsidiary factual particulars from the source’s account when the summary states the legal proposition without relying on those particulars.

all_of: The source supplies factual or evidentiary details beyond the facts needed to identify the legal issue and result.

preserve: If a factual detail is retained, preserve its accuracy and any qualification that makes it material to the stated legal distinction.

skills.name: Compress evidentiary particulars
skills.action: Compress witness-level testimony and evidentiary particulars into the material evidentiary conclusion, rather than reproducing the proof item by item.

all_of: The source recounts witness testimony, documentary proof, or other detailed evidence bearing on a proposition.

preserve: Keep an evidentiary fact when the summary uses it to state the material factual basis or a condition of the holding.
Do not turn a summary’s abbreviated account of proof into a claim that the source contained no further evidence.

skills.name: Use party roles instead of unnecessary proper names
skills.action: Refer to litigants and individual actors by their legally relevant roles or descriptions rather than carrying forward their proper names when the name is not needed to state the proposition.

all_of: The source identifies a litigant or individual actor by a proper name.
The source supplies a legally relevant role, relationship, or description for that actor that is sufficient to identify the actor in the holding or factual distinction without using the proper name.
exclude_if: The identity itself is a legally significant part of the source’s holding or distinction.

preserve: Retain the role, relationship, or institutional identity needed to understand the holding.
Retain a proper name if identity is legally significant or needed to distinguish actors.

skills.name: Omit nonoperative numerical particulars
skills.action: Leave out case-specific dates, amounts, and counts when they are granular narrative details rather than conditions of the summarized rule; retain numerical or temporal limits when they define the legal proposition.

all_of: The source provides specific dates, quantities, or monetary amounts for the underlying events or claim.
The source presents those particulars as facts about the case’s events, transactions, or claim, rather than as terms or limits of a statute, contract, grant, or other rule being applied.

preserve: Preserve a date, amount, or count if it is itself part of the legal rule, a material condition, or a qualification in the summary.

skills.name: Condense extended reasoning to its operative rationale
skills.action: Condense extended explanation of the court’s own reasoning to the operative rationale needed to state the rule or result.

all_of: The source develops a holding through multiple steps of explanatory reasoning, policy discussion, or application.

preserve: Retain reasoning that states a material condition, exception, or link between the rule and its application.
Do not replace a qualified holding with a broader one when condensing its explanation.

skills.name: Omit nonoperative background and rhetorical discussion
skills.action: Omit contextual or rhetorical discussion—such as historical scene-setting or evaluative commentary—when the summary states the operative rule or holding without it.

all_of: The source includes historical background, policy context, or evaluative or rhetorical discussion.
The source also states an operative rule or holding that can be summarized without that discussion.

preserve: Retain contextual material if the summary uses it to explain a necessary element of the rule or the reason for the result.
Do not omit the operative legal consequence merely because it is stated alongside background or rhetoric.

skills.name: Omit extended advocacy and rhetorical debate
skills.action: Leave out extended advocacy, dissenting debate, and rhetorical commentary when presenting the court’s summarized rule or result.

all_of: The source contains separately identifiable advocacy, dissent, or extended rhetorical discussion alongside a court rule or result.
exclude_if: The available source material is principally a party’s written argument and does not provide a distinct court rule or result to summarize.

preserve: Do not present an advocate’s or dissenting proposition as the court’s holding.

skills.name: Compress case-event dates
skills.action: Compress dates of case-specific events, rather than recounting a dated event-by-event sequence.

all_of: The source supplies dates for multiple events in the particular dispute, such as the grant, appeal, payment, or evidentiary events.

preserve: Retain dates that define an express statutory deadline, legal period, or other material temporal condition.

skills.name: Omit incidental numerical granularity
skills.action: Omit incidental exact quantities and measurements from the factual narrative when the summary states the rule at a more general level; do not round, alter, or detach a quantity from its source context if retaining it.

all_of: The opinion includes exact amounts, rates, durations, or measurements in its factual or illustrative discussion.
The source places the quantity in case-specific factual material, while stating the applicable proposition as a general legal rule that does not depend on that quantity.

preserve: If an exact amount, rate, duration, or measurement is retained, state it accurately and preserve what it measures.
Do not omit a quantity when it is necessary to express the summarized proposition.

skills.name: Omit extended background discussion
skills.action: Leave out extended historical or rhetorical background when the summary can state the relevant legal proposition without it.

all_of: The supplied source text contains extended historical, treaty, or event background that is distinct from legal analysis or a stated rule or disposition.
exclude_if: The source view is incomplete and does not provide enough source content to distinguish that background from the court’s legal analysis or stated rule or disposition.

preserve: Do not omit a historical or contextual fact if the summary relies on it to explain the rule or result.

skills.name: Compress statutory enactment background
skills.action: Leave out the detailed enactment sequence, statutory text, and legislative background when the summary states the operative legal proposition or consequence without them.

all_of: The source recounts multiple statutes, amendments, repeals, or statutory provisions as background to the decision.

preserve: If the summary states a statutory rule or consequence, preserve the source's meaning and the relevant qualification.
Do not require enactment dates, statutory citations, or statutory history when the source information is unavailable.

skills.name: Omit hypothetical illustrations
skills.action: Omit counterfactual or hypothetical illustrations when stating the determination, rather than reproducing the illustrative scenario.

all_of: The source uses a hypothetical, counterfactual, or imagined scenario to illustrate or support its legal reasoning.

preserve: If the summary retains the legal proposition illustrated by a hypothetical, state that proposition accurately without implying that the hypothetical facts occurred.

skills.name: Compress nonstatutory record quotations
skills.action: Omit or paraphrase extended quotations from testimony, agency findings, or procedural submissions instead of reproducing their wording; this pattern concerns record or narrative quotations, not operative statutory text.

all_of: The source includes an extended quotation from testimony, an agency finding, or a procedural submission.
The quoted passage is not itself the operative statutory language being construed.

preserve: Preserve the substance of a quoted passage when it supplies a fact or procedural point retained in the summary.
Do not apply this pattern to operative statutory language when the summary uses that language to state the legal basis.

skills.name: Paraphrase extended quoted legal text
skills.action: Compress extended quoted statutory or jury-instruction language into a statement of its operative meaning, retaining any short quoted term that carries a material condition.

all_of: The source reproduces an extended passage of statutory language or a jury instruction relevant to the ruling.
exclude_if: The source contains no extended quoted statutory or instructional passage.

preserve: Retain the quoted term or condition when it defines the operative boundary of the rule.
Preserve the instruction’s or statute’s material qualifications when paraphrasing.

skills.name: Omit opening case-framing before the propositions
skills.action: Begin with the legal propositions rather than reproducing the source’s opening case-identification, procedural, or advocacy framing.

all_of: The source opens with case-identification, procedural, or advocacy framing before presenting substantive legal propositions.

preserve: Retain procedural posture or case-specific context when it bears on a stated legal determination; the pattern concerns preliminary framing, not material procedural facts.

skills.name: Omit extended quotation and argument presentation
skills.action: Omit extended quoted material and the detailed presentation of party contentions when the synopsis can state the court’s resulting rule directly.

all_of: The source includes extended quotations, party contentions, or a detailed account of arguments.

preserve: If stating a party contention or quoted material is necessary to accurately convey the holding, retain its substance without suggesting that the court adopted the contention.

skills.name: Omit collateral precedent discussion
skills.action: Omit collateral precedent citations and case-history detail when stating the governing proposition; a closely relevant authority may still be named when the summary treats it as part of the proposition.

all_of: The source discusses multiple authorities or prior decisions, including material collateral to the source's governing proposition.
exclude_if: The source contains no supporting authorities or prior-decision discussion.

preserve: If a cited authority is retained, preserve its relationship to the proposition and do not imply that the source adopted a broader rule than it did.

skills.name: Omit record-level evidentiary and operational particulars
skills.action: When the source supplies detailed evidentiary or operational particulars—such as production quantities, payment figures, or the mechanics of a transaction—summarize the legal consequence without reproducing those record-level details.

all_of: The source excerpts give concrete evidentiary, operational, or quantitative particulars relevant to the dispute.
The source excerpts expressly state a legal rule or disposition, distinct in their text from those particulars.

preserve: If a specific quantity, amount, or operational fact is retained, preserve its accuracy and the qualification the source gives it.
Do not omit a factual detail when doing so would change the stated legal consequence.

skills.name: Compress intermediate procedural and administrative history
skills.action: Compress intermediate procedural or administrative history into the resulting legal proposition instead of recounting each prior step in the matter.

all_of: The source excerpts describe multiple procedural or administrative events preceding the court’s stated conclusion.
The source excerpts state a legal conclusion that can be expressed without narrating every preceding event.
exclude_if: The source excerpts provide only docket identifiers or scheduling information, with no substantive conclusion.

preserve: Retain the operative legal conclusion and any procedural qualification that changes the result.
If the procedural history is included, keep the sequence and attribution accurate.

skills.name: Omit separate-opinion reasoning from the holdings digest
skills.action: When the source includes a separately expressed dissent or other separate opinion, generally omit its reasoning from a digest of the court’s holdings rather than presenting it as part of the court’s operative conclusions.

all_of: The source excerpt includes a separately expressed dissent or other separate opinion.

preserve: If a separate opinion is mentioned, distinguish its position from the court’s holding.
Do not treat omission of a separate opinion as evidence that it was absent from the source.

skills.name: Lead with the legal propositions
skills.action: Lead with one or more declarative legal propositions that state the governing rule or the court’s central conclusion, rather than opening with a narrative account of how the case began.

all_of: The source presents a legal dispute and develops a rule, conclusion, or holding.

preserve: Keep the proposition accurate to the source and do not imply that every summary must begin with the same kind of holding.

skills.name: Keep distinct propositions separate
skills.action: Present distinct rules, applications, or conclusions as separable propositions or paragraphs; preserve distinctions between issues instead of merging them into an undifferentiated narrative.

all_of: The source addresses more than one legally distinguishable rule, issue, or application.

preserve: Retain the distinctions that affect the legal result; numbering is not required.

skills.name: Arrange extended analysis as digest propositions
skills.action: Arrange multiple independent legal propositions as a sequence of digest points rather than retelling the source’s extended discussion in its original chronology.

all_of: The source excerpt develops multiple legal propositions across an extended discussion.

preserve: Keep propositions that address distinct issues distinct; do not imply that sequence alone establishes a relationship between them.

skills.name: Separate distinct holdings
skills.action: Present separately resolved legal propositions as distinct entries rather than merging them into one undifferentiated statement.

all_of: The source resolves more than one distinct legal proposition or separately addresses multiple issues.

preserve: Keep each proposition faithful to the issue it addresses; do not imply that separate holdings have identical predicates or scope.

skills.name: Keep distinct rulings distinct
skills.action: When the source resolves more than one distinct legal issue, state the separate rulings as distinct propositions rather than collapsing them into one generalized conclusion.

all_of: The source excerpt addresses at least two distinct legal issues or claims.
The source gives a resolution for each issue.
exclude_if: The source excerpt presents only one resolved legal issue.

preserve: Represent each issue and its ruling accurately; do not imply that one ruling resolves a separate issue.

skills.name: Keep distinct rulings distinguishable
skills.action: When the source resolves multiple distinct legal propositions, state them as distinguishable clauses or successive sentences rather than blending them into one undifferentiated conclusion.

all_of: The source presents more than one independently material legal conclusion or rule.

preserve: Preserve the relationship among propositions, including whether one qualifies, explains, or is separate from another.

skills.name: Distinguish separate holdings in the presentation
skills.action: Present materially distinct holdings as separate propositions, using separate sentences or a sequence; numbering is one observed option, not a required format.

all_of: The source resolves more than one independently stateable legal issue or holding.

preserve: Keep each proposition faithful to its own issue and qualification; do not imply that separate holdings are parts of one broader rule when the source treats them independently.

skills.name: Connect decisive predicates to their legal consequences
skills.action: State the decisive record or procedural predicate together with the legal consequence the court attaches to it, rather than presenting the predicate as an unconnected fact.

all_of: The source ties a case-specific fact, record condition, or procedural act to a legal consequence.
The source states or applies that link in the court’s reasoning.

preserve: Preserve the source’s direction of the link: a predicate that supports a consequence must not be recast as defeating it, or vice versa.
State a causal or conditional link only when the source makes that connection.

skills.name: Group propositions by legal subject
skills.action: When the source presents several propositions on different legal subjects, group propositions addressing the same subject together rather than alternating among them as the source’s narrative proceeds.

all_of: The source presents multiple legal propositions on distinct subjects, along with a case narrative, evidentiary discussion, or procedural history.

preserve: Keep each proposition’s conditions and relationship to the relevant legal issue intact when grouping it.

skills.name: Declarative statement of a question-framed issue
skills.action: When the opinion frames the issue as a question, express the answer as a declarative legal proposition rather than preserving the question form.

all_of: The source frames a central legal issue as a question.

preserve: State the legal answer accurately and retain any qualifications that define its scope.

skills.name: Disposition follows the substantive propositions
skills.action: When reporting a formal disposition, place it after the substantive holding propositions rather than leading with it.

all_of: The source expressly states a formal disposition.
The source states one or more substantive holding propositions.

preserve: If the disposition is stated, preserve its result accurately; this convention concerns its placement, not whether every summary must include it.

skills.name: Close with the stated disposition
skills.action: Place the source's stated case disposition at the end of the summary when the opinion states one.

all_of: The source states a disposition of the case, such as granting a writ or affirming or reversing a judgment.

preserve: If stating the disposition, accurately report the outcome in the source; do not infer a disposition not stated there.

skills.name: Order retained procedural events chronologically
skills.action: When representing a source’s sequence of procedurally consequential events, present the retained steps in their procedural order.

all_of: The source describes multiple procedurally consequential events in a discernible sequence.

preserve: Keep the relationship between procedural steps and their legal consequences accurate.

skills.name: Separate independent propositions
skills.action: When the source resolves distinct legal propositions, state them as separable propositions instead of merging them into one undifferentiated rule.

all_of: The source resolves or expressly addresses more than one legally distinct proposition.

preserve: Keep propositions distinct only when they express different holdings or legal consequences; do not split one proposition into redundant paraphrases.

skills.name: Keep related holdings or consequences distinct
skills.action: Present separately stated rules or consequences as distinct propositions, commonly putting the principal holding before its application or related consequence.

all_of: The source resolves more than one legal issue, or states a principal rule together with a separate legal consequence or qualification.

preserve: Retain the relationship between a rule and its consequence or application.
Keep separate outcomes separate where combining them would obscure which legal question each answers.

skills.name: Arrange propositions as a legal digest
skills.action: Present the summary as a sequence of separate declarative legal propositions, each stating a rule, application, or qualification, rather than as a chronological retelling.

all_of: The source contains multiple legal propositions or a rule with related applications.

preserve: Keep each proposition’s relationship to the others intelligible, especially when one proposition qualifies or applies another.

skills.name: Lead with governing propositions before application
skills.action: Where the summary covers both a governing rule and its treatment in the case, generally present the rule before the case-specific application or procedural qualification.

all_of: The source addresses a general legal rule and also its application to the dispute.

preserve: Keep any qualification that changes the reach of the rule alongside the proposition it qualifies.

skills.name: Sequence independent holdings as propositions
skills.action: Present distinct holdings as successive propositions, allowing the synopsis to move from one resolved issue to another without reproducing the opinion’s chronology.

all_of: The source addresses more than one independently resolvable legal proposition.

preserve: Keep each proposition’s legal meaning distinct; do not imply that separately stated holdings depend on one another unless the source makes that connection.

skills.name: Separate multiple holdings and rule categories
skills.action: Represent distinct holdings or legally different categories as separate propositions when the source resolves more than one, rather than collapsing them into one undifferentiated rule.

all_of: The source resolves multiple independent legal propositions or expressly distinguishes multiple categories governed by different rules.
exclude_if: The source states only one operative proposition.

preserve: Keep the source’s distinctions between propositions or categories accurate; do not imply that a rule for one category governs another.

skills.name: Keep distinct propositions distinct and ordered
