skills.action: When the source presents separate claims or legal propositions, state them in a correspondingly ordered sequence rather than blending them into one undifferentiated conclusion.

all_of: The source addresses more than one distinct claim, question, or legal proposition.

preserve: Preserve which proposition applies to which claim or question.
Do not make a reserved question sound decided.

skills.name: Separate independent rulings
skills.action: When the source resolves multiple independent propositions, state them as distinct declarative propositions, commonly in successive sentences, rather than blending them into one narrative.

all_of: The source resolves at least two independently describable legal questions or rulings.

preserve: Keep each proposition tied to its own issue and source conditions.
Do not imply that distinct rulings share a condition or consequence unless the source does.

skills.name: Link threshold rule to operative circumstance
skills.action: State the governing threshold rule and connect it to the case’s operative circumstance or procedural consequence.

all_of: The source states a legal rule bearing on the court’s authority to review or entertain the matter and applies that rule to the case.

preserve: Preserve the rule’s stated conditions and the source’s actual application; do not generalize a case-specific result into an unconditional rule.

skills.name: Move from general rule to case application
skills.action: Arrange related propositions from the general rule or statutory construction to its application or consequence in the case.

all_of: The source states both a general legal proposition and a case-specific application or consequence.

preserve: Retain the source’s connection between the rule and the result when stating both.

skills.name: Sequence separate propositions directly
skills.action: When the source resolves multiple legal propositions, present them as successive declarative propositions rather than narrating the opinion’s sequence of discussion.

all_of: The source separately resolves more than one legal proposition.

preserve: Keep distinct propositions and their qualifications distinguishable; do not imply that separately stated propositions have identical scope.

skills.name: Preserve outcome-relevant legal categories
skills.action: Retain distinctions between legally different categories when the court's reasoning or result turns on that distinction, rather than collapsing them into a single broad category.

all_of: The source distinguishes two or more legal categories, capacities, or classes that affect the issue or result.

preserve: Keep the categories and the consequence attached to each category accurate; do not imply that the source treats them as interchangeable.

skills.name: Represent parties by legally relevant roles
skills.action: Describe parties by the legal role relevant to the proposition—such as stockholder, officer, surety, telegraph company, railroad company, or drainage commission—rather than carrying forward personal or corporate names when the role is what matters.

all_of: The source identifies parties by name or role and expressly makes their legal capacities material to the dispute.

preserve: Keep legally distinct capacities distinct when they affect the proposition; role-based description should not imply that different parties or capacities are interchangeable.

skills.name: Preserve material legal terminology
skills.action: Retain conventional legal or procedural terms when they express a material category or distinction; avoid replacing those terms with a less precise general paraphrase.

all_of: The source uses a legal, procedural, or doctrinal term to describe a rule, issue, or disposition, and the source itself treats the distinction that term denotes as material.
exclude_if: The source mentions a technical term only incidentally and does not explain or rely on the distinction it denotes.

preserve: Use a retained term consistently with the distinction made in the source; do not infer additional consequences merely from the term.
Do not retain incidental technical vocabulary solely for its own sake.

skills.name: Tie legal consequences to their operative predicates
skills.action: State the material predicate together with the legal consequence it triggers, so the proposition does not read as an unconditional rule detached from its operative circumstances.

all_of: The source connects a legal consequence to a stated factual, contractual, or procedural predicate.

preserve: Retain the source's stated trigger or limiting circumstance when expressing the consequence, and do not turn a case-specific application into a broader categorical rule.

skills.name: Preserve evidentiary and modal force
skills.action: Preserve the source’s degree of certainty: distinguish an established fact from a presumption, inference, record-based failure of proof, or conditional possibility.

all_of: The source describes a proposition using evidentiary uncertainty, a presumption or inference, a failure of the record to establish something, or a conditional possibility.

preserve: Do not convert a presumption into a factual finding or a conditional possibility into an accomplished event.
When the proposition turns on what the record establishes, preserve that record-based character rather than assert the underlying event as an independently established fact.

skills.name: Distinguish controlling holdings from dissenting views
skills.action: When the source distinguishes the court's controlling opinion from a dissent, report the controlling legal propositions as the digest's holdings rather than presenting a dissenting view as the court's rule.

all_of: The source excerpt contains both a court holding and a separately identifiable dissent or separate opinion.

preserve: Do not attribute a dissent's proposition to the court as a whole; preserve a separate opinion's stance if it is itself material to the proposition being summarized.

skills.name: Retain outcome-relevant limits on the rule
skills.action: State a material boundary on a rule when the source makes the outcome depend on that boundary, such as jurisdiction, location, timing, or the parties’ legal relationship.

all_of: The source expressly connects the legal result to a stated jurisdictional, temporal, geographic, or party-based limit.

preserve: Keep the stated boundary attached to the proposition it qualifies; do not broaden the rule beyond the source.

skills.name: Keep operative conditions attached to the rule
skills.action: When the rule depends on a particular circumstance, retain that circumstance in the proposition or its immediate context.

all_of: The source ties a legal conclusion to identifiable facts, statutory language, notice, timing, or procedural circumstances.

preserve: Do not turn a fact-specific result into a broader rule than the source supports.
Preserve material conditions such as notice, timing, the relevant location, or the kind of statutory authorization when the proposition depends on them.

skills.name: Keep express limits attached to legal rules
skills.action: State material limits on a rule alongside it, including temporal, notice, or forum-law conditions when those limits are part of the source's holding.

all_of: The source expressly makes a legal rule depend on a stated temporal, notice, or jurisdictional condition.

preserve: Include only conditions supported by the source, and preserve whether a condition is part of the rule, an issue for the factfinder, or a case-specific application.

skills.name: Paraphrase statutory text as an operative rule
skills.action: Paraphrase operative statutory language in terms of its legal scope or consequence rather than reproducing the statute’s full wording.

all_of: The source quotes or closely sets out statutory text.
The source also explains the text’s operative legal scope or consequence.

preserve: If paraphrasing, retain statutory conditions or limits that define the rule’s reach, such as the covered class or the status of the land.
Do not treat a statutory citation or an exact statutory phrase as required when the summary expresses the operative scope another way.

skills.name: Keep actor-status and setting limits on legal rules
skills.action: Retain qualifications about the actor’s legal status, capacity, or relevant setting when those qualifications delimit the reach of the stated rule; do not state the rule as applying to a broader class than the source supports.

all_of: The source’s legal conclusion is expressly tied to an actor’s legal status, capacity, or setting.

preserve: State the material status or setting accurately when retained.
Do not convert a case-specific qualification into a broader rule about all actors or settings.

skills.name: Distinguish contentions from judicial resolutions
skills.action: When the source separates a party’s contention from the court’s resolution, report the contention as a contention or focus on the adopted resolution; do not present an argument as a finding or holding.

all_of: The source excerpt presents a party’s or counsel’s position separately from a judicial resolution of the issue.

preserve: Attribute a position to the party or counsel when including it, and distinguish it from the court’s adopted conclusion.
Do not imply that a party’s contention was decided unless the source states that the court adopted it.

skills.name: Preserve legally operative timing
skills.action: Retain an operative date, period, or sequence when the legal consequence depends on when an event occurred; express the relevant relationship between events rather than listing dates as background.

all_of: The source makes a date, time period, or sequence of events material to a legal rule or outcome.
exclude_if: Dates in the source are merely historical or descriptive and do not affect the legal analysis or result.

preserve: If a timing detail is retained, keep its date, duration, and relationship to the legally relevant event accurate.
Do not treat a date as a general legal requirement when it is only a case-specific cutoff.

skills.name: Attribute determinations to the institution that made them
skills.action: When a proposition reports a determination or action that the source assigns to an agency, executive officer, or lower court, identify that actor in the digest rather than attributing the determination solely to the reviewing court.

all_of: The source expressly attributes a relevant finding, ruling, or action to an institution or official distinct from the reviewing court.

preserve: Distinguish the source of an agency or lower-court determination from the reviewing court’s own holding, and do not attribute a factual finding to an actor the source does not identify.

skills.name: Use compact party labels in propositions
skills.action: When stating a rule or conclusion, refer to the litigants by a compact role label or abbreviated name where that identifies their legal position; do not carry full party names into every proposition.

all_of: The source identifies individual parties by name.
The source states a proposition that can be expressed by reference to a party’s litigation or legal role.

preserve: Keep the party’s legally relevant role clear; do not use a role label that changes who bears a right, duty, or burden.

skills.name: Use legally salient role labels for actors
skills.action: Refer to litigants and other actors by their legally relevant roles or institutional identities when those labels suffice, rather than repeating full personal names.

all_of: The source names litigants or other actors and states their roles in the dispute.

preserve: Keep distinct actors distinguishable where their separate roles matter to the proposition.
Do not replace an identity with a role label if the identity itself is material.

skills.name: Calibrate the stated force of legal propositions
skills.action: Match the proposition’s expressed force to the source: preserve when the court describes a matter as discretionary or justified, and state a required consequence as mandatory only when the source supports that force.

all_of: The source distinguishes among discretionary authority, a justified course, or a required legal consequence.

preserve: Do not weaken a source-stated requirement into mere discretion or strengthen a discretionary or justified action into a categorical command.

skills.name: Use legally relevant roles or categories in place of case-specific identities
skills.action: Describe case-specific parties, tribunals, or groups by the legal role or category that matters to the stated proposition, rather than carrying over their individual names or case-specific labels.

all_of: The source's own holding or reasoning identifies a party, tribunal, or group by a legal role or category, and that role or category is material to the source's stated rule or disposition.
exclude_if: The source's own holding or reasoning makes a specific party's individual identity or named institution material, rather than merely identifying who participated.

preserve: Retain an identity or institutional name when it is itself material to the proposition.
Keep the summarized role or category consistent with the source.

skills.name: State role-dependent party distinctions
skills.action: Identify parties by the legal capacity or role that governs the proposition, rather than reducing a role-dependent rule to an undifferentiated reference to the parties.

all_of: The source distinguishes parties by legal capacity, status, or transaction role.
The stated rule or result depends on that distinction.

preserve: If the source makes liability or entitlement depend on a party’s status, retain the relevant status and its legally material qualification.

skills.name: Retain express temporal and valuation boundaries
skills.action: State an express temporal or valuation boundary when it defines the legal test or measure of relief, rather than replacing it with a generalized outcome.

all_of: The source defines finality, liability, or relief by an express point in time, valuation point, or comparable boundary.

preserve: Retain the source’s stated reference point and do not substitute a different time or measure.

skills.name: Use legally relevant party roles in place of unnecessary names
skills.action: Identify parties in the factual setup by their legally relevant roles (such as owner, physician, corporation, or purchaser) rather than reproducing their names when those names are not needed to state the proposition.

all_of: The source identifies parties by proper names or case-specific labels.
The source states a party's legally relevant role or relationship in connection with facts bearing on the legal issue.

preserve: If parties are described by role, preserve which role each party occupies and the legally material relationship among them.

skills.name: Attribute rules to their stated legal authority
skills.action: Name the jurisdiction or statute as the source of a rule when the human summary frames the proposition as arising from that particular legal authority.

all_of: The source expressly identifies a jurisdiction, statute, or other legal authority as the basis for the rule being summarized.

preserve: Keep the attribution accurate to the jurisdiction or authority identified in the source; do not imply that a jurisdiction-specific rule is universal.
Include an authority attribution only when the source provides one.

skills.name: Retain conditional and modal force
skills.action: Preserve the source's conditional or modal force when stating a legal proposition, including qualifications about when a rule applies or whether a result may follow.

all_of: The source states a legal proposition with an express condition, qualification, or modal term.

preserve: Do not turn a possibility into a certainty or remove a condition that limits the proposition's application.

skills.name: Refer to participants by legal or procedural role
skills.action: When the source narrates identifiable participants, describe them by their operative legal or procedural capacity, or collectively as a role group, instead of carrying through incidental personal names or individualized descriptions.

all_of: The source identifies participants by personal names or individualized descriptions and also makes their legal or procedural roles observable.
exclude_if: The participant’s personal identity is itself part of the stated legal issue or holding.

preserve: Keep distinct capacities distinct when the source assigns them different actions or legal significance.
Do not replace an identity with a role where the identity itself matters to the issue or holding.

skills.name: Retain material legal provenance
skills.action: Identify the governing legal source or regime when the source makes it material to the proposition, such as a named statute or a jurisdiction’s law.

all_of: The source identifies a particular statute, enactment, or jurisdiction’s law as the basis or scope of the proposition.

preserve: If the summary states a proposition whose scope or basis depends on the identified source of law, retain the relevant attribution accurately; do not imply that a jurisdiction-specific or statutory rule is universal.

skills.name: Retain the boundary on negative conclusions
skills.action: When stating a negative conclusion, keep it attached to the source’s stated evidentiary, temporal, or procedural boundary rather than broadening it into an absolute rule.

all_of: The source states a negative conclusion whose scope is limited by an evidentiary, temporal, or procedural condition.

preserve: If retaining the negative conclusion, preserve the source’s stated limit on what the evidence establishes, what a later decision changes, or what permits dismissal.
Do not turn a conclusion about a specific ground or time into a broader proposition about all grounds or times.

skills.name: Attribute consequential acts to their actors
skills.action: Keep consequential acts and decisions attributed to the actor or court that performed them, especially where the actor's authority or procedural role bears on the result.

all_of: The source identifies different actors or courts performing procedural or legally consequential acts.
The source makes an actor's role, authority, or decision relevant to the dispute.

preserve: Do not attribute an act or decision to a different actor than the source identifies.
Retain the actor's legally material role or authority when the summary includes the act.

skills.name: Retain limits on the reach of a holding
skills.action: Keep limits that define the reach of a proposition—such as the parties, issue previously decided, relevant time, or procedural stage—attached to the summarized result.

all_of: The source states a result whose reach depends on a defined issue, party, time period, or procedural stage.
The source supplies that limiting condition in its explanation or holding.

preserve: Preserve source-supported limits that materially narrow who may claim the result, what issue it resolves, or when it applies.
Do not convert a case-specific qualification into a universal rule.

skills.name: Paraphrase quoted legal rules
skills.action: When the source states a rule in quoted statutory or contractual language, express the retained proposition in paraphrased legal prose rather than reproducing an extended quotation.

all_of: The source contains quoted statutory or contractual language relevant to the summarized proposition.

preserve: Retain the legal effect of the quoted language if the proposition is included.
Keep statutory or contractual wording verbatim when its precise text is itself the issue being summarized or paraphrase would alter its meaning.

skills.name: Preserve controlling legal categories and test language
skills.action: Retain the governing legal or statutory category, test, or term when it is the distinction on which the proposition turns.

all_of: The source makes a technical legal category, statutory term, or test central to the issue or holding.

preserve: State the legal category or test accurately in its source context; retaining terminology does not require verbatim quotation.

skills.name: Procedural vehicle when scope-bearing
skills.action: Name the procedural vehicle or posture when it is material to the stated rule or result.

all_of: The source’s rule or result depends on a procedural vehicle, such as habeas corpus, certiorari, mandamus, or an appeal.

preserve: Do not imply that the same rule governs a different procedural vehicle if the source ties it to the stated one.

skills.name: Preserve express limits on the holding
skills.action: Retain qualifications that mark an issue as undecided, distinguish an actor's conduct from government action, or leave a policy determination to another branch.

all_of: The source expressly limits the court's decision or distinguishes the scope of a legal proposition.

preserve: Keep qualifications attached to the particular issue or proposition they limit; do not turn an expressly unresolved question into a decision or omit a stated boundary on the court's reasoning.

skills.name: Retain material boundaries on a stated rule
skills.action: When stating a rule, retain material limits that define its reach, such as a statutory condition, the relevant class, or an expressly unresolved issue.

all_of: The source expressly qualifies the scope of a legal rule or identifies a boundary on what is decided.
The source states a legal rule and expressly ties its reach to a stated condition, class, procedural posture, or unresolved issue.

preserve: Do not generalize a holding beyond the statutory conditions, class, procedural posture, or unresolved questions stated in the source.

skills.name: Report propositions impersonally
skills.action: Use an impersonal reporting stance to state legal propositions, rather than carrying over the source judge’s personal or rhetorical self-reference.

all_of: The source excerpt uses first-person judicial commentary or personal evaluative language.

preserve: Preserve the court’s legal position and any attribution necessary to distinguish a holding from a party’s argument.

skills.name: Impersonal legal-summary register
skills.action: Use an impersonal, formal statement of legal propositions rather than addressing the reader or presenting the author’s personal view.

all_of: The source excerpt includes first-person, audience-directed, or advocacy language.

preserve: Preserve attribution or dissent status when it is necessary to identify whose proposition is being summarized.

skills.name: Use an impersonal legal-digest voice
skills.action: Report legal conclusions in an impersonal, categorical digest voice rather than as a first-person account of the court's deliberation.

all_of: The source states a judicial ruling or legal conclusion.

preserve: State the court's conclusion without changing its attribution or presenting a party's contention as the court's holding.

skills.name: Use formal impersonal legal prose
skills.action: Use an impersonal, formal legal-summary voice, stating rules and conclusions directly rather than addressing the reader conversationally.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion represented in the reporter-style case-summary genre shown by these pairs.

preserve: Keep any attribution to the court accurate; this register does not require a particular introductory phrase or wording.

skills.name: State resolved propositions impersonally
skills.action: Render the court's resolved proposition in impersonal holding language rather than carrying forward the opinion's first-person account of its reasoning.

all_of: The source uses first-person judicial language in stating or reaching a resolved legal proposition.
exclude_if: The source excerpt contains no first-person judicial statement tied to a resolved proposition.

preserve: Keep the court's conclusion attributable to the court and do not convert a party's argument or a tentative statement into a holding.

skills.name: Retain identifying legal terminology
skills.action: Retain a concise doctrinal term or legal category when it identifies the rule or issue being summarized, rather than flattening that category into an imprecise general paraphrase.

all_of: The source uses an identifiable legal term of art or doctrinal category in stating a rule or resolving an issue.

preserve: Use a legal term only when the source supports that category, and do not broaden or alter its legal meaning.
Treat this as a choice of expression, not a requirement to include every technical term appearing in the source.

skills.name: Compact use of legal terminology
skills.action: Use established legal terms as compact labels for doctrines or legal categories, rather than adding a lay explanation of those terms.

all_of: The source states a legal rule or category using an established legal term.

preserve: Use a legal term only where it accurately describes the source's rule or category.
Retain qualifications that limit the term's application.

skills.name: Use impersonal declarative legal prose
skills.action: Express rules and outcomes in impersonal, declarative legal prose rather than addressing the reader or narrating a personal reaction.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion stating a legal rule, ruling, or disposition.

preserve: Retain any attribution needed to identify whose construction, ruling, or legal rule is being summarized.

skills.name: Impersonal reporting of judicial conclusions
skills.action: Render judicial conclusions in an impersonal, third-person summary voice rather than retaining the opinion’s first-person judicial phrasing.

all_of: The source opinion uses first-person judicial phrasing to state a conclusion or factual finding.

preserve: If stating the conclusion or finding, preserve its substance and scope accurately; changing the reporting voice does not authorize changing the court’s determination.

skills.name: Impersonal reporting of judicial conclusions
skills.action: Report the court’s reasoning in impersonal declarative terms; do not carry over first-person judicial narration or counsel’s advocacy as the summary’s own voice.

all_of: The source includes first-person judicial narration or a party’s argumentative position.

preserve: Preserve whether a proposition is the court’s holding or a party’s contention; do not recast advocacy as a judicial finding.

skills.name: Formal legal and procedural terminology
skills.action: Use the source-supported formal legal and procedural vocabulary characteristic of the summaries, rather than replacing it with a colloquial explanation.

all_of: The source states the relevant issue or procedure using recognizable legal terminology.

preserve: Use legal terms only where the source supports them, and retain their source-specific meaning.

skills.name: Use impersonal rather than first-person judicial narration
skills.action: State legal conclusions and reasoning in an impersonal voice rather than reproducing the opinion’s first-person judicial narration.

all_of: The source uses first-person plural narration by the court in its reasoning or conclusion.

preserve: Preserve the court’s actual holding and the distinction between its reasoning and the procedural outcome, if stated.

skills.name: Use impersonal legal reporting
skills.action: Recast first-person judicial assessment as an impersonal statement of the legal rule or case result.

all_of: The source expresses a legal conclusion using first-person judicial narration or assessment.
The source also supplies a rule or result that can be stated without that narrative framing.

preserve: Preserve the court's conclusion, its degree of certainty, and any stated conditions when removing first-person framing.
Do not attribute a proposition to the court if the source presents it only as a party's contention.

skills.name: Use impersonal declarative reporting
skills.action: Express legal propositions in an impersonal, declarative voice rather than adopting the opinion’s first-person judicial narration.

all_of: The source states the relevant rule or conclusion in judicial-opinion prose.
The source includes first-person judicial narration or an equivalent court-centered formulation.

preserve: If the court’s own assessment or reasoning is retained, do not attribute it to a party or present it as an independently established fact.

skills.name: Impersonal statement of the court’s conclusion
skills.action: Express the court’s resolution in impersonal, declarative terms rather than carrying over first-person judicial narration.

all_of: The source uses first-person judicial narration when discussing the court’s analysis or conclusion.
The source states a legal conclusion that can be expressed as a holding.

preserve: Preserve which conclusion the court reached and any limits stated in the source; changing the reporting stance should not change the substance.

skills.name: Use impersonal language for operative propositions
skills.action: Express the operative proposition in impersonal legal-summary language instead of retaining the court’s first-person deliberative phrasing.

all_of: The source presents an operative proposition using first-person judicial discussion, such as 'we think,' 'we can find,' or 'we will not say.'

preserve: Preserve the court's actual degree of certainty and any conditions or reservations; impersonal phrasing must not turn a tentative or conditional statement into an absolute rule.

skills.name: Impersonal rule statement
skills.action: Express the legal proposition in impersonal, rule-focused terms instead of reproducing the court’s first-person narration or framing it as what the court was asked to decide.

all_of: The source is an opinion that uses first-person judicial narration or frames the issue as a question before the court.
The source states a legal rule or conclusion that can be expressed independently of that narration.

preserve: If the proposition is stated, preserve the source’s legal meaning and any outcome-relevant qualifications; do not imply that the court adopted a proposition merely because it was presented as an argument.

skills.name: Impersonal case-reporting voice
skills.action: Report the court’s conclusions and procedural events in impersonal case-reporting prose, rather than adopting a litigant’s advocacy voice or reproducing first-person judicial narration.

all_of: The source includes first-person judicial narration, party advocacy, or formal court-order language.

preserve: Keep the court’s decision and any relevant party positions attributable to the correct actors.

skills.name: Retain conventional legal terminology
skills.action: Use conventional legal or procedural terminology for operative doctrines and steps, such as a demurrer, writ of error, appeal, or jurisdiction, rather than replacing those labels entirely with ordinary-language descriptions.

all_of: The source uses conventional legal or procedural terminology for an operative doctrine, procedural step, or review question.

preserve: Use legal terms consistently with their meaning in the source; do not imply a procedural event or jurisdictional result that the source does not establish.

skills.name: Neutral voice for judicial conclusions
skills.action: When the source states the court’s reasoning in the first person, recast the summary proposition in an impersonal or neutral declarative voice rather than narrating the court’s deliberation.

all_of: The source uses first-person judicial language to express a conclusion or reasoning.

preserve: Keep the proposition attributed to the court where needed, and preserve whether the court states a conclusion, a limitation, or an unresolved question.

skills.name: State propositions in an impersonal legal voice
skills.action: Use an impersonal, generalized legal register to state rules and conclusions, rather than retaining first-person judicial narration where the summary presents a proposition.

all_of: The source states a legal rule, conclusion, or holding in the court’s own voice.

preserve: Retain the court as the decision-maker where attribution is material; impersonal phrasing should not change who decided or what was decided.

skills.name: Use an impersonal legal-digest register
skills.action: Use an impersonal, declarative legal-digest voice to state rules and holdings rather than addressing the reader or adopting conversational commentary.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion that states a rule, holding, or case-specific application.

preserve: Keep evaluative or emphatic language only when it represents a material formulation in the source; report the court's position without adding a new one.

skills.name: Use an impersonal declarative register
skills.action: Use a formal, impersonal legal-summary voice, stating propositions directly rather than adopting the opinion's first-person deliberative voice.

all_of: The source contains judicial first-person deliberative narration, such as the court's use of “we think” or “we find.”

preserve: Keep the court's role and the status of a proposition clear; impersonal phrasing should not blur whether a statement is a holding or a party's contention.

skills.name: Use impersonal digest phrasing
skills.action: Use an impersonal, declarative digest voice for legal propositions rather than narrating the court’s deliberation or reproducing counsel’s argumentative stance.

all_of: The source uses first-person judicial evaluative language or deliberative commentary, such as “we think,” “the court is of opinion,” or “useless discussion.”

preserve: Do not alter whether a proposition is attributed to the court or a party when that attribution is legally material.
Do not treat the observed impersonal register as a requirement to omit a substantive dissent or separate opinion.

skills.name: Use declarative legal-report register
skills.action: Use a formal, declarative legal-report register to state rules and conclusions, rather than adopting the opinion’s rhetorical or conversational voice.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion containing legal analysis or argumentative language.

preserve: Preserve any attribution necessary to distinguish a court holding from a dissent or other speaker’s position.

skills.name: Declarative legal propositions
skills.action: Render the opinion’s legal conclusion as a compact, declarative proposition instead of reproducing its first-person or chronological exposition.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion excerpt that explains or applies a legal rule.

preserve: If stating a proposition, retain its legal meaning and any limitation expressed in the source.

skills.name: Use direct, impersonal legal prose
skills.action: Express the determination in direct, impersonal legal prose rather than carrying over first-person judicial voice or rhetorical emphasis.

all_of: The source uses first-person judicial voice, rhetorical phrasing, or extended judicial commentary.

preserve: Do not recast commentary as a separate holding or attribute a proposition beyond what the source supports.

skills.name: Impersonal reporting voice
skills.action: Use an impersonal case-reporting voice, stating rules and outcomes declaratively rather than addressing the reader or narrating an advocate's view.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion that states the court's disposition or holding on a legal issue.

preserve: Attribute the proposition to the court or mark it as a holding when needed to avoid presenting it as an unqualified statement of law.

skills.name: Use direct doctrinal statements
skills.action: State the legal proposition directly in declarative terms instead of framing the summary primarily as a narrative of what the court considered or said.

all_of: The source is an appellate opinion containing an express legal conclusion or rule.

preserve: Do not state a proposition more broadly than the source’s rule or conclusion.

skills.name: Use impersonal declarative summary language
skills.action: Use an impersonal, declarative case-summary voice rather than the source court’s first-person narration or argumentative exposition.

all_of: The source states its reasoning in a judicial opinion.

preserve: Do not alter the court’s level of certainty or attribute a proposition to a different decision-maker.
Retain a quoted legal formula when the summary genre uses it as operative text.

skills.name: Choose facts tied to the rule
skills.action: Select concrete facts that explain or delimit the legal proposition, while compressing other case-specific details.

all_of: The source provides factual circumstances that bear on the stated legal rule or its application.

preserve: If a factual circumstance is retained, preserve its material qualification and relationship to the rule; do not treat these examples as required facts in other cases.

skills.name: Retain distinct legal propositions in multi-issue decisions
skills.action: When the source addresses multiple independently resolved legal points, state the salient points as distinguishable propositions instead of flattening them into one undifferentiated holding.

all_of: The source presents more than one independently meaningful legal point, such as separate appeal issues, a threshold question and a merits question, or multiple controlling principles.
The source resolves at least two of those points.
exclude_if: The source presents only one material legal proposition.

preserve: Keep each retained proposition’s relationship to its issue or appeal clear.
Do not present a question the source leaves open as a resolved holding.

skills.name: Directly report the operative rule
skills.action: State the case’s operative legal holding or rule as a direct proposition, rather than making the reader infer it from the procedural narrative.

all_of: The source is an appellate opinion that states a legal ruling.

preserve: If reporting the holding, retain its scope and any stated limits or conditions; do not enlarge the rule beyond the source.

skills.name: State legal determinations as propositions
skills.action: Present the summary’s legal determinations as concise, declarative propositions rather than reproducing the source’s advocacy or extended case narrative.

all_of: The source discusses legal questions or determinations.

preserve: If a proposition is retained, preserve its legal meaning and the source-supported qualifications.

skills.name: Retain a concise factual anchor for instrument-based holdings
skills.action: Include a compact identifying feature of the instrument or transaction when it anchors the legal rule; do not reproduce every term or chronological detail merely because the source discusses it.

all_of: The source's legal issue turns on a particular instrument, property claim, or transaction whose identity is needed to understand the holding.

preserve: Keep the factual anchor accurate and proportionate to its role in the holding; do not treat any one training-case detail as mandatory.

skills.name: Distinguish the court’s resolution from competing positions
skills.action: When the source includes competing advocacy or a dissent alongside the court’s resolution, state the court’s adopted legal determination rather than presenting an advocate’s or dissenting judge’s position as the court’s rule.

all_of: The source presents competing legal positions, such as party arguments or a dissent, as well as a court resolution.
The source itself states a court legal determination on the same disputed matter raised by the competing positions.
exclude_if: The source excerpt contains no identifiable court resolution of the competing positions.

preserve: State the resolution only to the extent supported by the court’s own reasoning or disposition; do not attribute a litigant’s contention or dissenting view to the court.
Retain disagreement or a separate opinion when the proposition being summarized is specifically about that disagreement.

skills.name: Include the stated application of a rule
skills.action: When the source states both a general rule and its consequence for the affected party or class, include the consequence as well as the abstract rule.

all_of: The source states a general legal rule.
The source also states how that rule applies to a party or legally defined class in the case.

preserve: Keep the stated consequence tied to the source’s relevant class, condition, or procedural circumstance.
Do not imply that an application stated for one party or class governs beyond the source’s holding.

skills.name: Name the governing legal framework
skills.action: Identify the governing legal framework when the source expressly ties the resolved proposition to a statute, doctrine, or legal regime.

all_of: The source resolves a legal question and expressly identifies a governing statute, doctrine, or legal regime relevant to that resolution.
exclude_if: The source does not identify a governing legal framework for the proposition.

preserve: Identify the framework accurately and do not conflate distinct frameworks discussed in the source.
Do not add a citation or statutory detail that is unavailable in the source.

skills.name: Include the operative standard used to decide the dispute
skills.action: State the operative legal standard or threshold when the opinion uses it to resolve the dispute.

all_of: The source expressly states a standard, threshold, or test and applies it to resolve a legal issue.

preserve: State the standard at the level of generality used in the source.
Distinguish a governing standard from the court's application of that standard to the case.

skills.name: Express legally relevant roles instead of case-specific identities
skills.action: State parties, institutions, or property through the legal roles relevant to the proposition, rather than carrying forward their case-specific names or personal descriptions.

all_of: The source identifies parties, institutions, or property by specific names or case-specific descriptions.
The opinion resolves an issue by reference to their legal capacity or relationship.

preserve: Retain a party's legally material role or relationship when it defines the rule or its application; do not substitute a role that changes the source's meaning.

skills.name: Compress rejected arguments into the controlling answer
skills.action: State the controlling answer to an expressly presented rejected contention or alternative interpretation directly, rather than recounting the source’s argumentative path; include a concise negative qualification when it clarifies the answer.

all_of: The source expressly presents a party’s competing legal interpretation, contention, or objection.
The court resolves that contention or objection, and the resolution is relevant to the summarized rule.
exclude_if: The source does not expressly present and resolve a competing contention or objection.

preserve: If stating a rejection or qualification, preserve the court’s actual resolution and its scope; do not imply that a rejected contention was adopted.

skills.name: State the controlling legal classification
skills.action: State the legal classification that controls the result when the source distinguishes between competing categories, such as a business loss versus an investment loss or a statutory fee versus costs.

all_of: The source contrasts legal categories and explains that the distinction affects the rule or outcome.

preserve: Preserve the specific category and its legal consequence; do not suggest that a contrast exists unless the source supports it.

skills.name: Generalize the rule's subject
skills.action: Frame the selected rule around a general legal category or condition rather than leading with the named litigants and their case-specific events.

all_of: The source describes a specific dispute and also states a rule that applies to a recognizable category of cases, parties, or conditions.

preserve: Retain the legal and factual conditions that delimit the generalized rule.

skills.name: Holding-centered selection
skills.action: Select the opinion’s operative legal holding or holdings as the summary’s core, rather than making background narrative the organizing point.

all_of: The source states a judicial conclusion resolving a legal issue.

preserve: If stating a holding, retain its actual legal result and do not turn an example or subsidiary observation into a holding.

skills.name: Lead with an operative legal proposition
skills.action: State the operative legal conclusion or governing rule near the start of the summary, rather than making the reader reconstruct it from the source’s full sequence of argument.

all_of: The source is a judicial opinion that resolves at least one identifiable legal issue.

preserve: State the conclusion at the level supported by the source; do not turn a source-specific result into a broader rule.

skills.name: Condense extended reasoning
skills.action: Compress extended supporting analysis into a brief explanation connected to the stated rule or result, rather than reconstructing the source’s full reasoning.

all_of: The opinion develops a legal proposition through extended statutory, doctrinal, or factual analysis.

preserve: If the summary includes an explanation of why a rule applies, retain its stated legal basis and do not substitute a different rationale.

skills.name: Retain the rule’s case-specific application
skills.action: Include case-specific application or a concrete consequence of the governing rule when the source makes it part of the court’s resolution.

all_of: The source applies a legal rule to facts, a statutory scheme, or a procedural setting.

preserve: Do not present an application as a broader rule than the source establishes; retain material case-specific limits.

skills.name: Center the court’s resolution rather than the parties’ arguments
skills.action: Give priority to the court's resolving legal proposition over a narrative of the parties' competing contentions.

all_of: The source presents a legal dispute and states the court's resolution of it.

preserve: If a contention is included, distinguish it from the court's holding and state the court's resolution accurately.

skills.name: Compress extended source exposition
skills.action: Condense extended opinions into a brief digest of their decisive propositions instead of reproducing the full factual narrative and reasoning.

all_of: The source contains extended factual, procedural, or analytical discussion beyond the propositions needed to state the decision.

preserve: Compression should not remove qualifications that define the holding or change the source's stated result; no fixed word count is implied.

skills.name: Anchor propositions in the procedural or triggering setting
skills.action: State the operative legal proposition with its relevant procedural vehicle or triggering setting when that setting frames the rule; compress the surrounding case narrative.

all_of: The source identifies a procedural vehicle, posture, or factual trigger that frames the legal proposition.

preserve: Retain the source's actual procedural vehicle and any trigger that affects the rule; do not substitute a different posture or make a contextual detail a general requirement.

skills.name: Omit expressly unadjudicated questions
skills.action: Omit an issue the court expressly says it does not reach or need not decide, rather than presenting it as an additional holding.

all_of: The source expressly describes a legal question as unnecessary to determine, not arising, or otherwise not reached.
The source separately states a legal proposition that the summary can report without resolving that reserved question.

preserve: Distinguish an issue expressly left open or unnecessary to reach from a question the court resolves negatively.
Do not imply that the omitted issue was decided, rejected, or resolved by the proposition that is retained.

skills.name: Omit granular offense-investigation narrative
skills.action: Condense underlying offense and investigative history when the legal dispute turns on a particular challenged investigative method, retaining the challenged method and the procedural path relevant to its review.

all_of: The source contains a detailed underlying-offense or investigation narrative.
The legal issue under review concerns a distinct investigative method or constitutional question.

preserve: The investigative method directly challenged in the case.
Procedural facts needed to understand how that challenge reached the reviewing court.

skills.name: Omit supporting analogies when stating the operative holding
skills.action: Compress supporting reasoning into the governing rule and result rather than reciting the source's analogies to other legal doctrines or authorities.

all_of: The source gives a holding supported by analogies to other doctrines or authorities.
Those analogies are not independently necessary to identify the rule or its result.

preserve: The holding and the legal predicates material to it.
Any qualification needed to avoid changing the rule's scope.

skills.name: Compress procedural history to the legally operative issue
skills.action: In a concise statement of the legal issue, omit extended record-level facts and lower-court procedural detail when the source itself identifies a narrower legally operative status and issue.

all_of: The source contains extended factual or procedural history before expressly framing a narrower legal question.
The source frames that question in terms of a legally salient status or circumstance.

preserve: The status and circumstance that define the legal question.
Any procedural detail needed to understand the question being presented.

skills.name: Consolidate parallel cases around their shared rule
skills.action: When the source presents parallel cases on the same legal question, summarize their shared rule in one proposition instead of reproducing each case's separate factual and procedural narrative.

all_of: The source expressly presents multiple cases as addressing the same legal question.

preserve: The common legal question and its resolution.
Any qualification needed to express the shared rule accurately.

skills.name: Compress detailed property classes into their shared category
skills.action: Where the source separates property into procurement or storage classes and gives detailed handling facts, summarize the shared category and omit the item-by-item inventory and logistics unless they alter the stated issue or result.

all_of: The source gives multiple factual classes of property or goods relevant to a single tax dispute.
The source identifies the covered property under a shared general category and then supplies class-specific item inventories or handling details.

preserve: The general nature of the goods subject to the tax.
Any distinction between classes that is necessary to the stated legal basis or outcome.

skills.name: Omit administrative-burden policy support
skills.action: Omit policy arguments about administrative burden when the summary states the governing rule for discretionary review without those supporting arguments.

all_of: The source resolves the scope or availability of appellate review.
The source supports that resolution with policy arguments about burdens on court proceedings or administration.

preserve: The operative appellate-review rule.

skills.name: Omit expressly non-determinative subsidiary findings
skills.action: Omit a subsidiary agency finding when the source expressly says that the finding's presence or absence is not determinative of the outcome.

all_of: The source identifies a subsidiary or additional finding.
The source expressly characterizes that finding as not determinative.

preserve: Do not suggest the omitted finding was the basis for the decision.
Retain any independently stated controlling ground for the outcome.

skills.name: Generalize the purpose of an ancillary remand
skills.action: When a remand accompanies an otherwise sustained conviction, it may describe the remand’s purpose generally rather than reproduce the specific sentencing circumstances and corrective instructions.

all_of: The source sustains or affirms the principal result and also remands the case.
The source gives a specific reason or task for the remand.

preserve: The existence of the remand
Its connection to purposes stated in the opinion

skills.name: Omit the general-taxation caveat while keeping the holding tax-specific
skills.action: Keep the holding limited to the challenged flat license tax; omit the source’s separate clarification that general taxes may still apply.

all_of: The source distinguishes a targeted license tax on protected activity from generally applicable taxes.
The source’s holding concerns the targeted license tax.

preserve: That the holding concerns the flat license tax at issue, not a general exemption from taxation.

skills.name: Compress collateral preclusion background to the relevant private interest
skills.action: Compress collateral history about the underlying dispute and asserted preclusion theory when the summary can identify the relevant private interest without recounting how that theory arose.

all_of: The source recounts an asserted preclusion theory against companies that were not parties of record to the underlying judgment, and explains the theory through their alleged membership in a group that pooled defense resources and shared legal representation.

The source describes the court’s issue and disposition as concerning expenses for the investigation or amici participation, and identifies the companies’ connection to the judgment through their interest in the patents involved.
exclude_if: The source decides whether the companies were bound by the underlying judgment, or makes the details of the asserted preclusion theory necessary to explain the court’s ruling.

preserve: The existence of a private interest connected to the judgment under investigation

skills.name: Exclude superseded eligibility dispute
skills.action: Omit an earlier beneficiary-eligibility dispute when the source identifies the remaining issue on remand as the validity or meaning of a separate regulation.

all_of: The source describes an earlier dispute over whether a claimant qualified to be a beneficiary under the governing statute.
The source states that, after a remand, the issue remaining for decision is the validity or meaning of a distinct regulation.

preserve: The later issue that controls the appeal or decision on remand

skills.name: Omit the conservation rationale from the compact holding
skills.action: Omit the substantive conservation rationale when stating the regulatory holding.

all_of: The source explains a regulation’s application across producers by reference to conservation or a shared resource.

preserve: The operative as-applied result, without implying that the summary has recited the court’s full reasoning.

skills.name: Omit procedural standing history in a merits-focused digest
skills.action: Omit the administrative standing history and the lower court’s inferred resolution of procedural defects when summarizing the merits holding.

all_of: The source recounts an agency or appellate standing dispute before addressing the merits.
The source ultimately resolves the substantive legal challenge.

preserve: The substantive holding; do not imply that the omitted procedural history was resolved differently.

skills.name: Docket-style compression of continuance orders
skills.action: For an order continuing a proceeding while awaiting clarification of whether the judgment rests on an adequate independent state ground, reduce the account to a brief docket-style statement of the continuation and its calendar status; omit the legal uncertainty and the reason for awaiting clarification.

all_of: The source is a procedural order continuing a proceeding pending clarification of an adequate independent state ground.

preserve: That the proceeding was continued.

skills.name: Omit superseded procedural-route disputes when mootness resolves the action
skills.action: When intervening events make the ultimate dispute moot, the summary may omit earlier disputes over the proper court configuration and appellate or mandamus routes, and focus on the mootness resolution.

all_of: The source contains earlier procedural disputes or routes.
The source resolves the action on a later mootness ground.

preserve: The later mootness ground and resulting disposition.

skills.name: Omit detailed regulatory thresholds and locations
skills.action: Omit detailed state-by-state locations and numerical regulatory thresholds when the summary can identify the relevant class of violation and state the holding without them.

all_of: The source supplies jurisdiction-specific locations or numerical regulatory thresholds.
The source frames the principal issue at the general level of fines for violations of state maximum-weight laws and presents the jurisdiction-specific limits separately as factual context.

preserve: The general type of regulatory violation relevant to the holding.
Any jurisdiction-specific or numerical detail necessary to define the legal rule, if the source makes it essential.

skills.name: Omit ancillary in-forma-pauperis grant
skills.action: When the source separately grants an in-forma-pauperis motion alongside certiorari, omit the ancillary in-forma-pauperis grant while retaining the certiorari disposition.

all_of: The source separately states that an in-forma-pauperis motion and a petition for certiorari are granted.

preserve: The grant of certiorari and the operative disposition.

skills.name: Compress antecedent certified-question history
skills.action: Omit the antecedent procedural step that certified questions were answered, when summarizing the resulting certiorari disposition.

all_of: The source describes questions certified to another court and reports that they were answered before stating the resulting disposition.

preserve: The operative certiorari disposition and its improvidently-granted qualification.

skills.name: Omit granular confession-circumstance evidence
skills.action: Omit detailed trial-level evidence about how the confession was obtained when compressing the case to its voluntariness-hearing rule and remedy.

all_of: The source recounts trial testimony describing circumstances in which a confession was obtained.
The source addresses the remedy for an inadequate voluntariness hearing without deciding whether the confession was voluntary.

preserve: The fact that confession voluntariness is the subject of the procedural dispute
Any evidentiary detail necessary to state the holding accurately

skills.name: Omit a conditional government concession
skills.action: When the source states that a government advocate conditionally concedes the remedy if the court finds a legal defect, omit that advocacy statement when the summary directly states the court’s own holding and disposition.

all_of: The source attributes a conditional concession about the remedy to a government advocate.
The court itself resolves the underlying issue and states the disposition.

preserve: The court’s own resolution and disposition, not the advocate’s conditional position.

skills.name: Compress multi-factor doctrinal analysis to its result
skills.action: When explaining why a records doctrine does not apply, it is permissible to report the result without restating each factor of the source’s doctrinal analysis, particularly where the summary identifies the governing doctrine and cross-references related authority.

all_of: The source identifies the required-records doctrine and states whether it applies to the dispute.
The source gives a multi-factor analysis or states multiple premises bearing on the doctrine’s applicability.
exclude_if: The source makes a particular factor, qualification, or boundary essential to defining the scope of its conclusion, rather than merely explaining the doctrine’s application.

preserve: The identity of the doctrine and the holding on its application.
Any qualification necessary to avoid overstating the holding.

skills.name: Omit extended rebuttal of an administrative justification
skills.action: In a concise account of the holding, omit extended discussion of an asserted administrative rationale and its rebuttal when the summary states the resulting equal-treatment rule and required opportunity.

all_of: The source presents an administrative-burden justification for treating a foreign corporation differently from domestic corporations and addresses an equal-protection challenge to that treatment.

preserve: The governing equal-treatment rule
The required opportunity to establish eligibility under local law

skills.name: Omit a separate rebuttal based only on interstate travel
skills.action: In a state-remedy adequacy decision, the summary may state the controlling remedy finding without separately recounting the rejection of inconvenience based solely on having to litigate across a state line.

all_of: The source considers whether a state remedy is adequate under the Tax Injunction Act.
The source separately rejects the argument that crossing a state line makes an otherwise adequate remedy inefficient.

preserve: If stating the adequacy conclusion, do not imply that geographic inconvenience alone defeats it

skills.name: Omit the transferred local-cause jurisdiction pathway
skills.action: When explaining why an alternative statutory jurisdictional pathway does not control, omit its inapplicability explanation if the summary instead focuses on the statutory grant relevant to the holding.

all_of: The source discusses multiple statutory jurisdictional clauses.
The source explains that a clause providing jurisdiction over local causes is inapplicable because jurisdiction was transferred elsewhere.

preserve: The statutory jurisdictional ground that resolves the issue.
Do not imply that an inapplicable alternative clause was the basis for the decision.

skills.name: Compress collateral policy rationales for confidentiality
skills.action: Compress collateral explanations for why confidentiality may help a commission when the source's dispositive analysis instead turns on whether criminal punishment of nonparticipants is justified; retain the general legitimate-interest premise if needed to frame that analysis.

all_of: The source provides multiple policy reasons for confidentiality, such as witness cooperation, protection from retaliation, or avoiding premature reputational harm.
The source's decision turns on the constitutionality of punishing speech rather than on whether confidentiality itself is useful or valid.
exclude_if: The detailed policy reasons are independently dispositive or necessary to explain the holding.

preserve: That confidentiality may serve legitimate interests, if material to framing the constitutional inquiry.
The distinction between confidentiality itself and the separate punishment of speech.

skills.name: Omit fact-specific recording-practice rebuttal
skills.action: Omit a detailed response to a counterargument based on differences between human operators and automated systems or on whether particular calls are recorded, when the summary states the broader voluntary-conveyance and assumed-risk rationale.

all_of: The source presents a counterargument based on differences in a third party’s recording or retention practices.
The source also supplies a broader rule or rationale addressing voluntary conveyance to that third party.

preserve: The broader rationale that voluntary conveyance to a third party defeats the asserted expectation of privacy

skills.name: Omit the distinct over-objection mistrial framework when not at issue
skills.action: When the source distinguishes mistrials requested by the defendant from mistrials over the defendant’s objection, focus the summary’s governing-rule discussion on the posture at issue rather than reproducing the separate manifest-necessity framework for the other posture.

all_of: The source discusses both defendant-requested mistrials and mistrials over the defendant’s objection.
The case at hand concerns a mistrial requested by the defendant.

preserve: The governing rule for the procedural posture actually presented.
The distinction between defendant-requested and over-objection mistrials, if needed to make the rule clear.

skills.name: Omit extended interim-stay analysis
skills.action: Do not include an extended account of the general interim-stay assessment or law-of-the-case reasoning when the summary instead reports the operative procedural basis and disposition.

all_of: The source discusses factors supporting interim relief, such as prospects for merits review or success, or irreparable injury.
The source states a procedural threshold as the basis for entertaining or granting a stay and states the stay’s disposition and pending posture.

preserve: Do not suggest that the source’s stated reasoning was rejected or resolved differently.
Retain a specific factor if it is necessary to explain the disposition.

skills.name: Omit a time-barred merits-review route
skills.action: A concise procedural summary may omit a threshold time-limit rule that forecloses treating an application as a petition for merits review, when the summary instead reports the application’s disposition and procedural posture.

all_of: The source describes an application for an interim stay after state courts denied stays pending appeal, and the deciding court denies that application.
The source separately states that a missed deadline bars treating the stay application as a petition for merits review.

preserve: Do not imply that the underlying merits were decided if the source only forecloses a route to review them

skills.name: Omit conditional extraordinary-writ analysis
skills.action: A concise procedural summary may omit a separate extraordinary-writ avenue whose availability depends on whether the source identifies a risk that appellate review will become moot.

all_of: The source discusses an extraordinary writ under 28 U.S.C. § 1651 in aid of appellate jurisdiction.
The source ties whether such a writ may issue to whether the appeal will become moot unless a stay is granted.

preserve: Do not suggest that extraordinary relief was categorically unavailable if the source states only that a condition for it was not shown

skills.name: Omit the separate professional-ethics analysis
skills.action: When the source rejects an ethical-duty theory and locates the issue instead in statutory interpretation, omit the separate ethics analysis while retaining the statutory holding.

all_of: The source distinguishes a professional-ethics argument from the statutory basis for deciding the fee-waiver issue.

preserve: Do not characterize the result as turning on counsel’s ethical duties when the source grounds it in the statute.
Retain the statutory basis for the disposition.

skills.name: Omit general evidentiary-discretion background
skills.action: Omit broad background qualifications about ordinary evidentiary discretion when the summary states the case-specific constitutional holding and the source’s applied rationale.

all_of: The source states generally that a trial judge makes many decisions concerning the admissibility of evidence.
The source also resolves a particular constitutional challenge to an evidentiary exclusion.

preserve: The case-specific constitutional holding and the facts or reasoning that support its application.
Do not imply that ordinary evidentiary discretion is absent; this omission describes the summary’s compression, not the governing law.

skills.name: Omit history deemed inconclusive in favor of textual reasoning
skills.action: Omit extended legislative-history discussion when the source treats it as inconclusive and the operative text resolves the interpretive question.

all_of: The source discusses legislative history relevant to a statutory-interpretation issue.
The source expressly characterizes the results of the relevant legislative investigation as inconclusive and irrelevant.
The source resolves that same interpretive issue by relying on the operative statutory text.
exclude_if: The available source is partial and does not establish the scope of the history discussion or the source’s resolution of the interpretive issue.

preserve: The source’s controlling textual rationale.
Any material qualification that the source attaches to the role of legislative history.

skills.name: Omit unresolved sanctions sequencing
skills.action: Omit a separate lower-court sequencing issue about whether a discovery order is proper despite possible foreign-law violations and what sanctions might follow noncompliance, unless the reviewing court resolves or adopts that issue.

all_of: The source attributes to the Court of Appeals a two-stage treatment of objections based on the French penal statute: whether the discovery order was proper despite possible violations of French law, and what sanctions might follow inability to comply.

The supplied human summary is marked complete and reports the reviewing court’s holdings on Convention procedures and comity without stating that it resolved or adopted that separate sequencing-and-sanctions question.
exclude_if: The source or its complete human summary states that the reviewing court resolved or adopted the separate sequencing-and-sanctions question.

preserve: Do not imply that the reviewing court resolved the separate sanctions question.
Retain the issue if it becomes part of the reviewing court’s disposition or holding.

skills.name: Omit immaterial mechanics of alternative benefit options
skills.action: Compress detailed mechanics of alternative benefit options when the legally material point is that optional plans used sex-based calculations that reduced benefits for one group.

all_of: The source describes multiple optional retirement-benefit plans through detailed payment terms or contingencies.
The source identifies sex-based actuarial calculations as producing lower monthly benefits for one group.
exclude_if: The source treats the terms of a particular option as determining the claimed violation or remedy.

preserve: The existence of optional benefit structures
The discriminatory calculation and its effect on payments

skills.name: Compress peripheral security details around visibility
skills.action: Describe physical privacy measures at the level needed to explain the relevant viewing conditions, without reproducing peripheral property or security details that do not affect that explanation.

all_of: The source gives several physical-property details, while its reasoning turns on what could be seen from a particular vantage point.

preserve: The facts that explain ground-level concealment and aerial visibility

skills.name: Compresses a statutory stay condition
skills.action: When summarizing a statutory stay based on related litigation with nonparties, describe the stay rule or result without necessarily reciting the additional possibility-of-conflicting-rulings condition.

all_of: The source discusses a statutory stay of arbitration based on related litigation involving third parties not bound by the arbitration agreement.

preserve: Identify that the stay concerns related litigation involving parties not bound by the arbitration agreement.
Do not state or imply that the omitted statutory condition was rejected or inapplicable.

skills.name: Omit underlying merits detail in a later fee dispute
skills.action: Open with the case’s procedural path and the legally operative reason for the remand, rather than reproducing detailed medical or other underlying merits evidence when the issue being decided concerns a later fee award.

all_of: The source describes an underlying benefits or agency merits dispute followed by a separate fee-award issue.
The source includes factual details about the underlying merits that are not necessary to explain the fee issue.

preserve: The procedural event that makes the later fee dispute material, such as reversal and remand.
Underlying merits facts if they are necessary to understand the ruling on fees.

skills.name: Omit the equipoise-only practical-effect qualification
skills.action: Where the source expressly limits the practical effect of a burden allocation to cases in which the evidence is in equipoise, the summary may state the general holding without carrying forward that operational qualification.

all_of: The source separately states (1) a constitutional holding permitting a party to bear a burden of proof under a stated standard and (2) that the burden allocation affects determinations under the governing state law only when the evidence is in equipoise.
The supplied source view is complete.

preserve: The general holding on which party may bear the burden and the applicable standard.

skills.name: Compress collateral rules into a general reminder
skills.action: Group secondary evidentiary rules at a general level when the source discusses several collateral rules in addition to its principal admissibility rule, rather than reproducing each rule’s detail.

all_of: The source discusses multiple ancillary rules alongside a principal rule that drives the holding.
exclude_if: A particular ancillary rule supplies an independent ground for the result or is otherwise central to the dispute.

preserve: That other applicable rules remain relevant
Any ancillary rule that independently determines the outcome

skills.name: Compress individual inquiry findings
skills.action: When retaining a general conclusion that a required multi-part inquiry was not shown, omit the source's specific descriptions of individual threshold findings unless the summary needs them to state a distinct holding.

all_of: The source identifies a required multi-part inquiry, describes its individual threshold criteria, and states that the court gave no indication it undertook the inquiry.

preserve: The broader conclusion that the required inquiry was not shown

The connection between that chronology and the residence requirement.

skills.name: Concise merger-and-market setup

The source identifies the merging firms’ roles or positions in their respective markets.

preserve: The challenged transaction and requested remedy.
The parties’ distinct market positions when they are material to the case.

skills.name: Interindustry competition can receive § 7 protection

preserve: The legal point that distinct products or industry boundaries do not, by themselves, eliminate § 7 protection for competition.

skills.name: Use market indicators to recognize actual competition

The connection between that longer-run response and § 7 market definition.

skills.action: When witness process is requested at public expense and the source gives that expense as an independent discretionary ground, the summary may report the trial-delay and reviewability rule without separately stating the funding ground.
