The source identifies the expense of the process as an independent discretionary consideration, apart from delaying trial.

preserve: Distinguish the independent funding-based discretion from discretion to delay trial for witness production.
Do not imply that the summary’s delay rationale is the only basis stated in the source.

skills.name: Omit underlying evidence narrative when stating a reviewability rule
skills.action: When the appellate issue is resolved by a reviewability rule, omit the underlying evidentiary narrative unless needed to state that rule.

all_of: The source contains a detailed account of evidence underlying the verdict.
The source resolves the appellate challenge by stating a limit on review of the evidence.

preserve: The appellate review standard that resolves the challenge.
Any underlying fact necessary to make that standard intelligible.

skills.name: Omit alternative merits discussion after preservation disposes of argument claim
skills.action: When an argument-related claim is disposed of for failure to preserve an objection, omit the source’s alternative discussion of whether the argument itself exceeded proper bounds.

all_of: The source addresses a claim that an advocate’s argument was improper.
The source identifies a failure to preserve the objection.
The source also discusses whether the argument was improper on its merits.

preserve: The preservation rule and its consequence for the assignment of error.

skills.name: Compress certificate evidentiary mechanics
skills.action: When the source explains the evidentiary effect of a required certificate, the summary may state the certificate requirement without reproducing the separate rules about prima facie effect, exclusivity of evidence, or rebuttal.

all_of: The source specifies a required document’s evidentiary status or how its evidentiary effect may be challenged.
The source also states a broader rule requiring that document for a legal entitlement.

preserve: The requirement to produce the certificate and what it must establish.
Do not imply that the certificate is conclusive if describing its evidentiary effect.

skills.name: Omit individualized proof of a general-rule application
skills.action: When the source gives case-specific proof and application after stating a broader governing rule, the summary may omit that individualized application and state the rule instead.

all_of: The source states a statutory rule requiring a certificate or comparable documentation to establish eligibility, and separately states that the litigant did not produce the required certificate and did not account for its absence.

preserve: State the governing rule accurately if using it in place of the case-specific application.

skills.name: Summarize recovery claim without specifying its legal route
skills.action: Describe the purchaser’s claim at a high level as an action to recover the tax-sale purchase money, without detailing whether recovery is sought under common law or statute.

all_of: The source frames a monetary recovery claim arising from a tax sale.
The source distinguishes common-law recovery from a statutory route.

preserve: The purchaser sought return of the tax-sale payment.
The claim’s relationship to the tax sale.

skills.name: Omit superseded statutory history
skills.action: Omit historical statutory authorization and its supporting history when the summary states the operative monetary jurisdictional rule and result.

all_of: The source identifies a former statutory authorization for appeals or writs of error as no longer in force, alongside a distinct operative monetary jurisdictional threshold and its application to the writ.
exclude_if: The source's disposition turns on resolving a dispute about the former provision's continuing force, scope, or historical meaning.

preserve: The operative jurisdictional threshold and its application to the writ.

skills.name: Omit nonwaivability and sua sponte rule
skills.action: Omit the general rule that diversity jurisdiction cannot be waived and must be noticed by the court on its own motion when the summary reports the jurisdictional dismissal without giving that broader rule.

all_of: The source states that lack of diversity jurisdiction is nonwaivable or must be noticed sua sponte.
The source separately states a case-specific jurisdictional holding and disposition based on whether the parties are citizens of different states.

preserve: The case-specific jurisdictional holding, where included.
Do not imply that the general nonwaivability rule was rejected.

skills.name: Omit superseded award amount
skills.action: Do not carry forward the numeric amount of a rejected lower-court damages award when the summary gives the operative damages result instead.

all_of: The source identifies a specific lower-court monetary award.
The reviewing court rejects that award and states a different recoverable measure.

preserve: The operative damages result in place of the rejected award's numeric amount.

skills.name: Omit route-specific timing calculations from a concise holding
skills.action: In a concise statement of the jurisdictional holding, omit case-specific procedural dates and the detailed calculation of whether the writ was timely.

all_of: The source states a jurisdictional holding concerning review of a rehearing denial.

The source separately recounts a case-specific writ-timing calculation based on the judgment date and the period during which a rehearing petition remained pending through a transition from a territorial court to a state court.

preserve: The jurisdictional result
Any procedural transfer relationship necessary to identify the ruling under review

skills.name: Omit separate nonparty-creditor impairment rationale
skills.action: Omit the separate rationale that granting mandamus would divert funds already appropriated for creditors who are not parties, while preserving the dispositive statutory-right analysis.

all_of: The source identifies creditors or other right-holders who are not parties to the proceeding.
The source states that granting the requested relief would impair the contract rights of creditors who are not before the court.
The source also provides a distinct statutory basis for rejecting the claimant's asserted right.

preserve: The statutory basis for finding no enforceable contract right.
The holding on the requested mandamus remedy.

skills.name: Exclude speculative value evidence from the jurisdictional account
skills.action: Omit evidence or assertions about an invention’s potential commercial value when the source treats them as irrelevant to valuing the pending patent-application claim for jurisdiction.

all_of: The source discusses commercial-value evidence or assertions in connection with a jurisdictional valuation inquiry.
The source explains that such evidence does not establish the required value of the matter in dispute.

preserve: The distinction between actual value of the matter in dispute and speculation about the value of a potentially patentable invention

skills.name: Omit distinctions of prior jurisdiction precedents
skills.action: Omit reconciliation of earlier jurisdiction decisions when their different procedural routes or governing statutes explain why they do not control the present appeal.

all_of: The source raises an earlier jurisdiction decision as a suggested basis for jurisdiction.

The source identifies the statutory basis governing appeals from the Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia and discusses the § 4915 patent proceeding in connection with the earlier-decision discussion.

preserve: Do not imply that contrary precedent was ignored if the summary mentions the issue; preserve the governing-route distinction when needed to explain the holding

skills.name: Omit contextual narrowing of treaty land terms
skills.action: Omit the contextual interpretive analysis that narrows a treaty’s general land description through a geographic category supplied by the treaty.

all_of: The source interprets a treaty term describing eligible land by reference to a limiting geographic category in the surrounding text.

preserve: The summary may state the outcome without explaining the contextual construction of the treaty’s geographic limitation.

skills.name: Omit the distinct administrative-award jurisdiction argument
skills.action: Omit the separate argument that proceedings or an award by an administrative department enlarge the court’s jurisdiction, and the court’s response to that argument; state the statutory limit directly.

all_of: The source considers whether an administrative examination, allowance, or award changes the scope of statutory jurisdiction.

preserve: The summary’s statutory jurisdictional rule and its application to consequential damages.

skills.name: Condense supporting sovereign-immunity and constitutional analysis
skills.action: Omit the extended sovereign-immunity discussion, constitutional comparison, and cited authorities when stating the statutory holding.

all_of: The source identifies the claim as a purely statutory right and states that the Court of Claims’ jurisdiction cannot be enlarged by implication.
The source invokes the general principle that the government is not liable to suit without its consent while resolving the statutory claim.

preserve: The statutory boundary that controls the result.

skills.name: Omit the detailed in-rem and in-personam reach rules
skills.action: Omit the separate explanation that an in-rem judgment reaches only property within the rendering court’s control, while an in-personam judgment reaches parties and those in privity.

all_of: The source distinguishes the reach of in-rem and in-personam judgments as part of its reasoning about the effect of an estate appointment.
exclude_if: The source view is incomplete.

preserve: Retain the ultimate rule about the appointment’s nonconclusive effect even if the judgment-class analysis is omitted.
Do not suggest the omitted distinction was rejected; the summary simply does not state it.

skills.name: Omit the precise effective-date rule
skills.action: When the dispute turns on when a statutory readjustment based on returns takes effect, retain the general conclusion about the statute but omit the specific rule fixing effectiveness at the quarter after the returns.

all_of: The source interprets a statute that ties a financial readjustment to reported returns.
The statute or court specifies when the readjustment takes effect.

preserve: The general conclusion that the statutes govern the readjustment dispute.

skills.name: Omit the later enactment's rule for unresolved claims
skills.action: When a later enactment validates an administrative method and directs its use for unresolved claims, summarize the case's result without retaining that distinct legislative mandate.

all_of: The source discusses a later enactment addressing an administrative method previously used under an earlier statute.
The later enactment distinguishes unresolved claims from claims already resolved.

preserve: The summary's general statement that the governing statutes control.

skills.name: Compress coercion rebuttal into non-demand fact
skills.action: Compress a separate rejection of a coercion explanation into the broader fact that no payment demand was made, rather than recounting the source’s detailed rebuttal, when that rebuttal is not otherwise central to the summary.

all_of: The source expressly rejects a suggestion that the claimant was prevented by coercion or subordinate status from making a demand.

The source recounts that no demand was made to successive Bureau chiefs or Secretaries of the Treasury, and that the first demand was made in the petition more than fourteen years after the initial interview.

preserve: The prolonged absence of a demand, which the summary does retain

skills.name: Omit collateral unappealed rate orders
skills.action: Identify the challenged order without recounting earlier unappealed rate orders that the source distinguishes from it.

all_of: The source distinguishes the challenged regulatory order from other orders concerning similar rates.
The other orders are not the orders under review.

preserve: The identity or relevant scope of the order actually under review.

skills.name: Omit underlying injury facts when the appellate issue is statutory classification
skills.action: Omit underlying injury and negligence background when the summarized appellate issue is the constitutionality of a statutory classification and the source does not resolve the underlying injury merits.

all_of: The source includes facts about an underlying injury or liability claim.
The appellate issue addressed is the constitutionality of a statutory classification, rather than liability for the underlying injury.

preserve: Keep the constitutional classification issue and its holding; do not imply that the underlying injury or negligence claim was adjudicated on appeal.

skills.name: Omit merits details immaterial to review
skills.action: When the dispute is about appellate review rather than the underlying merits, omit trial-level details that do not affect the review question, while retaining any merits theory that supplies a jurisdictionally relevant argument.

all_of: The source describes a trial judgment on the underlying dispute and subsequent appellate proceedings.
The source decides whether the later state-court judgment is reviewable under Judicial Code § 237, including whether a federal question was properly presented or sufficiently asserted.
The source treats an underlying federal or constitutional theory as a possible basis for review, rather than resolving the underlying merits of the dispute.

preserve: Any underlying legal theory that bears on the review question

skills.name: Condense statutory hearing mechanics to the decisive guarantee
skills.action: When a statutory scheme contains detailed notice, objection, and hearing mechanics but the stated holding turns on the operative opportunity and authority to be heard, condense those mechanics to their legally decisive function rather than reciting each administrative step.

all_of: The source describes detailed statutory procedures for notice, objections, or administrative hearings.
The source’s resolution turns on the existence, authority, or timing of a hearing rather than on compliance with each procedural detail.
exclude_if: The validity of a particular notice, deadline, filing step, or hearing procedure is itself disputed or dispositive.

preserve: Preserve the legally material hearing opportunity, the board’s authority, and any material timing condition.
Do not omit procedural details that the source identifies as independently disputed or dispositive.

skills.name: Omit accident-specific injury reconstruction when abstracting the legal rules
skills.action: Compress a detailed accident narrative when the summary can present the governing legal propositions through the recurring hazard and the legally material employee-knowledge facts.

all_of: The source includes detailed individual accident or injury facts.
The source resolves a legal issue through a recurring hazard, a general standard, or a doctrine based on the actor’s knowledge.

preserve: Retain facts necessary to define the recurring hazard and the basis for the employee’s presumed knowledge.
Do not omit a fact if it changes the legal rule or the application of assumption of risk.

skills.name: Omit detailed procedural routes when they do not state the holding
skills.action: Compress or omit the detailed route and chronology of litigation when summarizing the substantive statutory holding, including separate suits, removal, supplemental pleadings, and the lower courts' handling of them.

all_of: The source describes a certificate application pending before a federal administrative commission and a separate state-court suit seeking to prevent the cessation of intrastate railroad operations during that pendency.
The source states a statutory holding about the commission’s authority over discontinuance of purely intrastate service.
exclude_if: The source makes the state suit, its procedural route, or its disposition a stated basis for or limitation on that statutory holding.

preserve: The substantive statutory holding and its scope.
Do not infer that procedural posture should be omitted when it affects the rule, issue presented, or disposition.

skills.name: Omit supporting trial-conduct particulars
skills.action: Compress detailed allegations about counsel's specific trial conduct into the controlling characterization of the trial when those details serve as support for the mob-domination claim rather than as separate holdings.

all_of: The source describes particular acts or omissions by trial counsel during a trial alleged to have occurred under mob pressure.
The source states a controlling due-process characterization of a trial conducted under mob domination.
The source presents the particular counsel-conduct details as support for the mob-domination or unfair-trial claim, rather than as independently resolved legal grounds.

preserve: Retain the legally material characterization of mob domination and denial of rights.
Do not imply that the specific omitted conduct was irrelevant to the source court's assessment.

skills.name: Set aside guilt issues when the question is trial fairness
skills.action: When the source expressly sets aside guilt or motive as not bearing on the constitutional trial question, omit those merits issues and focus the summary on preservation of trial rights.

all_of: The source expressly leaves the accused’s innocence or guilt aside because the question is whether their constitutional rights were preserved.
The source identifies preservation of constitutional trial rights, rather than the underlying merits, as the question to be addressed.

preserve: The source’s stated distinction between guilt or motive and the constitutional fairness question.
The procedural or constitutional issue actually being decided.

skills.name: Omit the implied-in-fact contract qualification
skills.action: A summary may state that jurisdiction covers express or implied contracts without also reciting the source’s further rule that an implied contract must be implied in fact.

all_of: The source limits a statutory contract-jurisdiction category by distinguishing implied-in-fact contracts from contracts implied in law.

preserve: The statutory contract-jurisdiction category at a high level
The ultimate jurisdictional holding

skills.name: Omit the tax-as-no-contract rationale
skills.action: The summary may omit the source’s explanation that a unilateral tax levy does not create a contractual promise by the party taxed.

all_of: The source rejects contract jurisdiction on the ground that a unilateral tax levy does not establish a contract or promise by the taxed party.

preserve: The jurisdictional result
The statutory contract category implicated

skills.name: Omit the separate accrued-liability consequence of revocation
skills.action: When summarizing a revocation that ended a law’s prospective operation, the human summary may report the revocation without stating the separate holding that liability for prior violations remains enforceable.

all_of: The source states that a proclamation was revoked.
The source expressly raises whether revocation affects prosecution or punishment for offenses committed while the proclamation was in force.

preserve: Do not imply that revocation necessarily extinguishes liability for prior violations.

skills.name: Omit extended territorial history when jurisdiction is dispositive
skills.action: Omit extended historical background about successive sovereigns, territorial governance, and cession when the summary instead centers on the jurisdictional issue and the provisions directly used to resolve it.

all_of: The source recounts a historical chain of territorial sovereignty or cession bearing on a claimed legal status or right.
The source expressly disposes of review on a threshold jurisdictional ground rather than deciding the underlying status or right.

preserve: The jurisdictional issue and its disposition.
Any historical detail necessary to understand the particular right or provision actually analyzed.

skills.name: Omit specified evidentiary vehicles while retaining the required showing
skills.action: When summarizing an amount-based jurisdictional proof requirement, the summary may state the burden and required showing without reproducing the source's specified evidentiary vehicles.

all_of: The source identifies particular evidentiary vehicles for establishing an amount-in-controversy jurisdictional fact.

preserve: That the jurisdictional fact must be established
The burden-bearer and applicable amount threshold, if summarized

skills.name: Omit a collateral bond-penalty argument
skills.action: A summary may omit a collateral argument that a bond's greater penalty does not change the amount-in-controversy analysis.

all_of: The source considers whether a bond's penalty affects an amount-in-controversy jurisdictional calculation.

preserve: The principal jurisdictional burden and value analysis, if included

skills.name: Omit a conditional opportunity for additional value proof
skills.action: A summary may omit a conditional opportunity to supply additional proof of value when it reports the present jurisdictional conclusion and disposition.

all_of: The source allows a party to establish additional value evidence conditionally or later.

preserve: The present jurisdictional assessment and disposition, if summarized

skills.name: Omit a deferral to related pending cases
skills.action: A summary may omit the source's deferral of related issues to other pending cases when those issues are not resolved in the summarized disposition.

all_of: The source defers consideration of related issues to other pending cases.

preserve: The disposition in the case being summarized, if included

skills.name: Compress detailed explanation of procedural noncompliance
skills.action: When a party’s procedural position rests on a general claim of having satisfied legal requirements, the summary may state that claim without reproducing a detailed account of an unexecuted clerk-provided form and the party’s explanation for not executing it.

all_of: The source gives a party’s explanation for a procedural failure.
That explanation includes specific clerical or document-handling details in addition to the party’s general claim of compliance.

preserve: The party’s material position about whether it had met the governing procedural requirements.
Any separately stated court-imposed condition or deadline for curing the procedural failure.

skills.name: Omit the ordinary-liability baseline when summarizing the directed-payment rule
skills.action: In a summary centered on a principal-directed exception, omit the general baseline rule governing a marshal’s responsibility for a deputy acting in execution of process when that baseline is not needed to state the exception.

all_of: The source states the marshal’s general responsibility for a deputy’s execution of process and expressly describes that responsibility in the circumstance where the deputy acted without the plaintiffs’ or their attorney’s orders.
The source separately states that when the deputy receives funds on the plaintiffs’ directions, the deputy acts as their agent and the marshal is not responsible for carrying out those directions.

preserve: The exception’s rule about the deputy acting on the principal’s directions.
Do not imply that the exception states the full rule for deputies acting without such directions.

skills.name: Compress a specific timing-condition dispute into the instruction rule
skills.action: Omit a subsidiary dispute about whether prompt payment was a condition of the deputy’s authority when the summary states the resulting responsibility rule at the broader level of disobeyed instructions.

all_of: The source recounts an argument that compliance with a specific timing condition was required.
The source resolves responsibility without making that timing dispute the basis of the stated rule.
exclude_if: The source view is incomplete.

preserve: The broader rule about responsibility when the deputy disobeys the principal’s instructions.
Do not present the alleged timing condition as a separately established holding.

skills.name: Omit dependent injunctive relief from the jurisdictional account
skills.action: Do not separately recount an injunction request when the source treats it as dependent on obtaining the underlying contract relief and the summary states the jurisdictional classification of that underlying claim.

all_of: The source describes the requested injunction as a consequence of a decree granting relief concerning the underlying contract or claim.
The source resolves appellate jurisdiction by classifying the underlying suit under specified jurisdictional categories and applying the amount-in-dispute threshold.

preserve: The jurisdictional basis and conclusion concerning the underlying contract claim.
Do not imply that the injunction supplied an independent basis for jurisdiction.

skills.name: Omit title-history particulars when statutory grounds resolve the claim
skills.action: When the summarized decision turns on statutory eligibility and the scope of a statutory remedy, omit detailed historical conveyance and survey particulars unless they independently affect those issues.

all_of: The source recounts detailed allegations of a grant or conveyance and an accompanying survey or figurative plan for the claimed land.

The source states that the statutory land-claim route requires residence in Louisiana by specified dates and does not cover perfect grants, placing such grants outside the District Court’s jurisdiction.
The source addresses substitute public-land relief for land allegedly sold or confirmed to others and states that there was no evidence the United States had made the asserted sales.

preserve: Any title-history detail that independently determines statutory eligibility, title completeness, or the availability of relief.

skills.name: Compress the general collateral-paper diligence rule when retaining the no-loss application
skills.action: If the source discusses a general diligence standard for a holder of collateral paper but resolves the dispute by finding no loss from the alleged lack of diligence, it may compress the general standard and retain the no-loss application.

all_of: The source discusses the diligence required of a holder of collateral paper or a comparable instrument.
The source also addresses whether lack of diligence caused loss to the underlying debtor or guarantor.

preserve: If summarizing the application, retain that absence of loss supports the conclusion on alleged negligence.
Do not imply that the source lacked a general rule about a collateral-paper holder’s duties.

skills.name: Omit broad judicial-noninterference rationale
skills.action: Omit the broader judicial-noninterference rationale when summarizing the appraisal ruling, while retaining the case-specific conclusion about the appraisal's validity.

all_of: The source gives a general rationale limiting judicial reexamination of an administrative valuation.
The source states that an inaccurate chemical-examination rule did not destroy the validity of the appraisement.

preserve: The case-specific conclusion that the challenged appraisal method did not invalidate the appraisement.

skills.name: Omit underlying conveyance dispute when the appellate issue is temporal
skills.action: When the controlling appellate issue is the effect of a later legal change on an earlier judgment, omit detailed title-chain evidence and the parties’ deed-characterization dispute unless needed to state that issue.

all_of: The source contains a fact-specific dispute over title or conveyance.
The source’s appellate resolution turns on whether a later legal change makes an earlier judgment erroneous.
exclude_if: The conveyance details independently determine the appellate outcome or are necessary to explain the governing rule.

preserve: The appellate rule about the effect of a later legal change on an earlier judgment.
Any conveyance detail independently necessary to understand that rule.

skills.name: Omit error-raising timing rule when summarizing the dismissal ground
skills.action: In a concise summary focused on the dismissal ground, omit procedural rules about when alleged errors must be specified or raised.

all_of: The source states that a party seeking review need not specify alleged errors on the record before argument, and that the errors are not brought to the court’s notice until argument.
The source denies a motion to dismiss a writ on the ground that no error appears on the face of the record, explaining that the merits must await final hearing.

preserve: The stated basis for the motion and its disposition.

skills.name: Omit alternative dismissal grounds not at issue
skills.action: When summarizing a ruling on one asserted dismissal ground, omit other grounds that the source identifies as permissible bases for dismissal unless they are at issue in the ruling.

all_of: The source identifies want of jurisdiction and irregularity of the writ as the only grounds for dismissal.
The source says the motion seeks dismissal because no error appears on the face of the record.
The source says deciding whether the record contains error would decide the legal merits, which must await final hearing rather than a motion to dismiss.

preserve: The dismissal ground actually addressed by the ruling.

skills.name: Omit merits-deferral rationale from the concise disposition
skills.action: Omit the explanation that deciding whether the judgment is erroneous would decide the merits when the summary states the ground-specific dismissal ruling.

all_of: The source explains that deciding whether the judgment is erroneous would decide the merits, which cannot be done on a motion to dismiss or quash.
The source denies dismissal on the asserted ground that no error appears on the face of the record.

preserve: The court's refusal to dismiss on the asserted ground.

skills.name: Omit the separate limitations-versus-categorical-bar analysis
skills.action: In a compressed statement of the holding, omit the separate analysis distinguishing an ordinary time-based limitation from a law that categorically denies an action on a judgment based on the underlying claim’s limitations status.

all_of: The source distinguishes a time-based limitations rule from a categorical bar on enforcing judgments from another State.
The source explicitly characterizes the challenged provision as denying efficacy of a judgment recovered in another State when the cause of action was barred under the forum State's limitations law.

preserve: Do not imply that ordinary limitation periods and categorical judgment-enforcement bars are the same rule.

skills.name: Omit case-specific evidentiary application when the source declines to reproduce facts
skills.action: When the source expressly declines to reproduce facts in a weight-of-evidence case, omit the case-specific evidentiary findings and application, while retaining the court’s stated approach to presenting those facts.

all_of: The source presents a fact-bound evidentiary question.
The source expressly states that it will not reproduce the facts on which its judgment rests.

preserve: The existence of the court’s fact-bound evidentiary assessment, at the level of its stated approach.
The distinction between the general approach and the specific facts or findings being left out.

skills.name: Omit disposition when summarizing only the evidentiary-recitation explanation
skills.action: When the summary focuses on the source's explanation of its evidentiary-only treatment, it may omit the resulting affirmance rather than add a separate disposition statement.

all_of: The source states that the question is wholly one of the weight of evidence and involves no controverted proposition of law.
The source expressly says it will not reproduce the facts on which its judgment rests.
The source states an affirmance after that explanation.

preserve: This omission is demonstrated in a summary centered on the court's explanation, not as a general rule that dispositions are unimportant.

skills.name: Sequence correction and related proceedings
skills.action: Present the sequence from discovery of a disputed contract term, through the offer to correct it and refusal, to the ensuing legal proceedings.

all_of: The source describes a proposed contract correction followed by separate or related proceedings over enforcement and equitable relief.

preserve: The sequence linking the correction dispute to enforcement litigation
The distinction between an action seeking royalties and an equity bill seeking cancellation or restraint

skills.name: Order rule, claimant status, and entitlement
skills.action: When the source presents a governing legal-status rule, a claimant-specific status determination, and an entitlement result, organize the summary in that progression: rule, claimant status, then result and its rationale.

all_of: The source resolves a claim that depends both on the status of a claimant group and on a governing rule about a collective entity or its property.

preserve: The governing legal-status proposition before the claimant-specific determination.
The entitlement conclusion after the status determination.
The rationale attached to the result.

skills.name: Signal a repeated prior insurance ruling
skills.action: Refer briefly to the prior decision's insurance determination as repeated, rather than restating its reasoning.

all_of: The source identifies an issue as already decided in a cited or earlier case.
The current case applies or repeats that prior determination.

preserve: Make clear that the insurance issue is resolved by reference to an earlier decision.
Do not imply that the present opinion supplies new reasoning on that issue.

skills.name: Move from application to general evidentiary rule
skills.action: Present the case-specific application first, then state the general rule governing parol evidence of a condition to effectiveness.

all_of: The source concludes that an instrument never went into effect, distinguishes the issue from contradicting or varying a written instrument by parol testimony, and identifies a recognized broader class of instruments whose operation depends on later events.
exclude_if: The source contains no distinct general rule beyond its case-specific conclusion.

preserve: The distinction between the case's outcome and the rule that explains its evidentiary basis.
The application-before-general-rule sequence.

skills.name: Jurisdiction challenge followed by amendment
skills.action: Present the procedural path through the jurisdictional demurrer and the plaintiff’s amended pleading before stating the holding.

all_of: The source describes a jurisdictional challenge followed by an amendment to the pleading.
The amendment is relevant to the issue ultimately decided.

preserve: The jurisdictional challenge.
The subsequent amendment relevant to the court’s resolution.

skills.name: Frame the issue through legally decisive chronology
skills.action: Frame the central issue with the legally decisive sequence of events when the source makes entitlement turn on the relationship between an allotment, the allottee’s death, a later agreement, and a post-agreement award or patent.

all_of: The source concerns an entitlement or title dispute involving an allotment and a later governing agreement.
The timing of the allotment, death, agreement, or later award affects the legal issue.

preserve: The event sequence that determines which legal regime applies.
The relationship between the stated chronology and the issue being decided.

skills.name: Summarize supervisory review and remand
skills.action: When a state high court uses supervisory review to set aside an intermediate appellate judgment and remand for decision, summarize the supervisory mechanism, the conflict or other stated basis for intervention, and the remand relationship.

all_of: The source describes a state high court exercising supervisory review over an intermediate appellate court.
The source identifies a basis for setting aside the intermediate court’s judgment and a remand.

preserve: The state supervisory-review mechanism
The reason the intermediate judgment was set aside
The remand to the intermediate court

skills.name: Explain finality through state review sequence
skills.action: When reviewability depends on the sequence of state-court proceedings, summarize the state supervisory action and explain why the later judgment is final for federal review, including the absence of further state review.

all_of: The source describes state supervisory review followed by a later state-court judgment.
Federal reviewability turns on whether that later judgment is final or further state review is available.

preserve: The relationship between state supervisory review and the later judgment under review.
Whether any further state review was available.

skills.name: Group delegated-authority rulings as a statutory package
skills.action: For a dispute about a legislature's delegated authority where federal statutes already tax an industry, organize the related statutory rulings together and distinguish the scope of the federal-law limitation, any implied license, and the authority for additional taxation.

all_of: The source addresses a local legislature's authority under a delegation statute.
The dispute concerns interaction between that authority and existing federal taxes or laws affecting an industry.

preserve: The distinction between the protected category of federal laws and federal tax provisions.
Whether an existing federal tax implies permission to continue the taxed business.
Whether the delegation permits additional local taxation.

skills.name: Separate the narrower loss-allocation ground
skills.action: State the breach-of-trust loss-allocation principle as a distinct proposition when the source uses it as a narrower ground for denying relief.

all_of: The source identifies a narrower or alternative ground for denying a requested remedy.
That ground allocates loss between innocent parties based on which party’s act of confidence enabled the breach of trust.

preserve: The parties’ innocence as stated in the principle.
The causal role of the act of confidence in enabling the breach.
The resulting allocation of the loss.

skills.name: Thematic organization of notice doctrines
skills.action: Organize the summary around general notice and waiver rules, followed by the specific demand exception for known insolvency, rather than recounting the source’s procedural sequence.

all_of: The source presents legal rules through procedural events, instructions, or multiple issues.
The source contains more than one distinct rule concerning notice, waiver, or demand.

preserve: Present rules as topical legal propositions rather than tracking the source’s sequence of trial instructions and appellate analysis.
Keep materially distinct notice, waiver, and demand rules distinguishable.

skills.name: Lead with the certified question's procedural posture
skills.action: Open with the certified legal question and identify the lower-court disagreement when the case arrives on a certified division.

all_of: The source presents a question certified from a lower court after a division or disagreement among judges.

preserve: The fact of a lower-court division and certification
The legal question placed before the reviewing court

skills.name: Retain the sequence and function of successive proclamations
skills.action: When the dispute turns on successive executive proclamations activating and later revoking a legal regime, briefly state their sequence and role as procedural or legal context.

all_of: The source describes successive executive proclamations affecting when a statutory or resolution-based rule operates.

preserve: Distinguish revocation of an implementing proclamation from repeal of the underlying law; do not infer that revocation necessarily extinguishes earlier liability.

skills.name: Retain the qualified jurisdiction ruling
skills.action: Retain the jurisdiction ruling when the source explains that a refused instruction concerned only credit items capable of reducing the debt below the jurisdictional threshold; preserve that limiting relationship rather than presenting the ruling as unconditional.

all_of: The source addresses a jurisdiction objection tied to the amount in controversy.
The challenged instruction applies only to credit items that could reduce the debt below the jurisdictional threshold.

preserve: The jurisdictional conclusion
That the instruction was limited to credits that could reduce the debt below the jurisdictional threshold

skills.name: Retain stated monetary figures relevant to jurisdiction
skills.action: When amounts bear on a jurisdictional threshold, retain the source’s stated balance and ad damnum rather than replacing them with a generalized description of the dispute’s value.

all_of: The source states both an amount in the declaration and an ad damnum.
The source discusses a jurisdictional amount threshold.

preserve: The stated balance and ad damnum when the source also addresses a jurisdictional threshold

skills.name: Track third-party participation and defense in review proceedings
skills.action: Summarize the procedural progression from a third party’s participation in a bill of review, through that party’s answer, to the reviewing court’s disposition; retain the party’s asserted lack of knowledge and purchaser status as procedural context.

all_of: The source describes a bill of review in which a third party is admitted as a defendant.
That party answers by denying or disclaiming knowledge of alleged fraud and asserts purchaser status.
The source reports the result of the bill-of-review proceeding.

preserve: The third party’s role in the review proceeding.
The substance of the party’s answer when it bears on the claimed interest.
The review court’s result, when reported.

skills.name: Retain express coverage of pending review bills
skills.action: Where a statute expressly covers bills already filed as well as bills to be filed, preserve that express temporal reach when summarizing the statute’s scope.

all_of: The source quotes or discusses statutory language covering bills filed before enactment as well as bills filed afterward.

preserve: The distinction between bills already filed and bills filed later, if the source makes it explicit.

skills.name: Material verdict-related claim item
skills.action: Foreground the bill-of-particulars item identified as material to the argument and decision, and connect it to the jury’s verdict.

all_of: The source describes multiple claims or bill-of-particulars items.
The source identifies a particular item as material to the decision or as the basis of the verdict.
exclude_if: The source does not distinguish a material or verdict-producing item from other claims.

preserve: Preserve which claim item mattered to the decision and its relationship to the jury’s verdict.

skills.name: Retain the certified-question path and answer
skills.action: When a case reaches a reviewing court through a certificate of division, retain the procedural chain that identifies the challenged issue as the point certified for decision, and report the reviewing court’s answer as resolving that point.

all_of: The source describes a lower court division of opinion and certification of a legal question to a reviewing court.

preserve: The lower-court division and certification of a specified legal question.
The reviewing court’s answer as directed to that certified question.

skills.name: Present administrative refund authority as potentially cumulative
skills.action: When both an administrative refund mechanism and a common-law action are at issue, preserve the argument that the refund mechanism supplements rather than extinguishes the action.

all_of: The source discusses an administrative official's authority to refund or repay money.
The source also discusses an existing judicial remedy for recovering that money.

preserve: The administrative refund mechanism's distinct function
The argument that it does not extinguish or suspend the judicial action

skills.name: Retain party-specific choice-of-law ground
skills.action: Include a separate choice-of-law ground explaining which jurisdiction’s law governs an obligor’s liability, even after addressing the law where performance was due.

all_of: The source considers whether the law of a drawee’s jurisdiction affects an indorser’s liability in a different jurisdiction, and identifies the jurisdiction where the indorser’s contract was made.

preserve: The governing law may differ for the drawee and for other parties to the instrument.
Identify the contract-related jurisdiction relevant to the liability at issue.

skills.name: Tie finality to the judgment’s operative effect
skills.action: Explain the finality analysis through the judgment's practical legal effect, including whether it leaves the affected party able to continue the challenged conduct.

all_of: The source assesses finality by examining the legal effect of the challenged judgment.

preserve: Whether the judgment actually bars, ousts, or otherwise prevents the relevant conduct
The connection between that effect and the conclusion on finality

skills.name: Identify the operative pleading-stage ruling
skills.action: Retain the demurrer and joinder posture when that pleading-stage ruling is the basis for the finality question.

all_of: The source’s finality issue arises from a ruling on a demurrer and the opposing party’s joinder in demurrer.

preserve: The demurrer to the pleading
The ruling’s procedural connection to the finality issue

skills.name: State the ruling on whether an informal verdict supports judgment
skills.action: When a verdict is informal or challenged as incomplete, state whether it nevertheless supports judgment by summarizing the court’s conclusion about the issues it resolved.

all_of: The source reviews whether a verdict adequately resolves the matters submitted for decision.

preserve: Distinguish informality from legal insufficiency.
Retain the court’s conclusion that the verdict supports judgment.

skills.name: Retain representative-gap facts tied to a distribution proceeding
skills.action: When the timing of an estate representative's appointment explains why an interested estate had no one to protect its interest during a distribution, retain that procedural chronology.

all_of: The source gives the timing of a party's death and appointment of an estate representative.
The interval overlaps a proceeding affecting the estate's interest.
exclude_if: The representative's appointment timing has no stated connection to notice, participation, or protection of the interest.

preserve: The fact that no authorized representative existed during the relevant proceedings, if established by the source.
The timing needed to show how that absence relates to the distribution.

skills.name: State whether remedy must be redirected to distributees
skills.action: When the claim is brought against a fiduciary who received or retained a distributed fund, state whether the claimant must instead pursue distributees; preserve any factual condition limiting that remedy choice.

all_of: The source addresses a claim against a trustee, executor, or administrator after distribution of a fund.
The source considers whether the claimant must proceed against distributees instead.

preserve: The distinction between a remedy against the fiduciary and a suit to recover from distributees.
Any case-specific qualification that makes redirection unnecessary.

skills.name: Retain the in-person enforcement alternative
skills.action: When the source describes an available in-person enforcement route as an alternative to the receiver’s direct suit elsewhere, retain the route of coercing the debtor to bring the property within the court’s reach or transfer it under the applicable law.

all_of: The source discusses equitable enforcement over property outside the court’s territorial jurisdiction.
The source identifies coercion of the debtor’s person or a conveyance as a means to enforce the court’s order.

preserve: The court may seek compliance from the debtor personally, including requiring the debtor to bring the property within the court’s jurisdiction or convey it in a legally effective manner.

skills.name: Preserve the receiver–bankruptcy-assignee distinction
skills.action: Distinguish a receiver under a creditor’s bill from an assignee in bankruptcy when explaining their claims to property across jurisdictions; preserve the contrast between the receiver’s court-derived role and the assignee’s statutory vesting, as well as the stated difference between English and United States treatment of bankruptcy assignments.

all_of: The source compares a receiver under a creditor’s bill with an assignee in bankruptcy.
The source discusses recognition of bankruptcy assignments across jurisdictions.

preserve: Do not treat a receiver’s court appointment as equivalent to statutory vesting in a bankruptcy assignee.
Where the source makes a jurisdictional comparison, retain the material difference in treatment across legal systems.

skills.name: Retain failure to pursue coercive process
skills.action: Include a material failure to use available in-person enforcement procedures when the court treats inaction as a reason the receiver’s claim does not prevail.

all_of: The source identifies an available procedure to enforce an injunction or decree against the debtor personally.
The source relies on the creditor’s or receiver’s failure to use that procedure in assessing the claimed right.

preserve: State when the creditor or receiver did not seek an available order compelling the debtor’s personal compliance, if that omission bears on the court’s reasoning.

skills.name: Summarize unsatisfied-judgment creditor-bill procedure
skills.action: Summarize the underlying enforcement sequence by identifying the unsatisfied judgment, the creditor’s bill seeking equitable assets, and the receiver’s appointment.

all_of: The source describes a creditor seeking equitable assets after an execution is returned unsatisfied.
A receiver is appointed in the creditor’s-bill proceeding.

preserve: The execution was returned unsatisfied.
The creditor sought equitable assets through a creditor’s bill.
The receiver’s appointment followed that proceeding.
